body:
## Summary

- **Bug fix** (`src/data.py`): `preprocess_dataset()` crashed when called from the evaluator mid-training with _"Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess"_.
- **Housekeeping** (`.gitignore`): expanded from 7 lines to a comprehensive default.

## What changed and why

### `src/data.py`

`DataModule.preprocess_dataset()` uses `datasets.map(num_proc=N)`. When `N > 1` on Linux (Kaggle, most training servers), the `datasets` library spawns workers via the default `fork` start method. If training has already started, CUDA is initialised in the parent process; forked children inherit that context and PyTorch refuses to continue:

```
RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess.
To use CUDA with multiprocessing, you must use the 'spawn' start method
```

**Fix:** check `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` at the top of `preprocess_dataset()` and set `num_proc = 1` when it returns `True`. This silently falls back to single-process tokenisation for any call that happens after the GPU is in use (i.e. every evaluation checkpoint), while preserving the configured parallelism for the cold initial preprocessing that runs before training.

```python
num_proc = 1 if torch.cuda.is_initialized() else self.config.num_proc
```

### `.gitignore`

Expanded the existing 7-line file to cover the full standard Python/ML development surface:
- Virtual environments (`.venv/`, `venv/`, `env/`, `.python-version`)
- Python bytecode & build artefacts
- IDE files (`.idea/`, `*.swp`, `.DS_Store`)
- Test/coverage tooling (`.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, etc.)
- Jupyter checkpoints
- Secret files (`.env`, `.env.*` with `!.env.example` exception)
- ML artefacts (`wandb/`, `lightning_logs/`, `*.pt`, `*.ckpt`, `*.bin`, `*.safetensors`)

## Test plan

- [ ] Run training on a GPU machine (Kaggle T4/P100) with `data.num_proc=4`; confirm evaluation no longer crashes after the first checkpoint.
- [ ] Run training with `data.num_proc=1` (default); confirm behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Verify `.gitignore` patterns catch `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, and `*.pt` files locally.

body:
## TLDR

Chirp relay diagnostics now display durable per-relay session EVENT counts instead of summing only currently retained wire-subscription rows. This fixes misleading zero counts after one-shot subscriptions are evicted.

## Overview

- Added `RelayStatus.events_rx` from the durable relay transport/session counters and regenerated the Swift projection type.
- Updated the relay diagnostics projection so top-level relay rows use durable session EVENT counts while per-wire-sub rows keep their own per-sub counts for detail views.
- Added a regression test for an indexer relay (`purplepag.es`) that has no retained sub rows but has received an EVENT, ensuring the row still shows a non-zero count.
- Split relay diagnostics display formatting/tone helpers into `relay_diagnostics/format.rs` to keep the touched projection file under the repo line-count ceiling.
- Documented the relay diagnostics acceptance criterion in the Chirp parity spec and V-51 backlog: zero counts must be explainable, and configured indexers must visibly participate in discovery-kind routing or explain why not.

## Decisions and tradeoffs

- I kept the TUI thin: it continues rendering Rust-owned projection fields and does not infer session counts from UI state.
- The top-level row now means “session EVENT frames received by this relay URL”; wire-sub detail rows remain the place for per-subscription counts. This is more honest after EOSE/CLOSED eviction.
- I did not add a new ADR or planning file. The docs update extends the existing V-51 observability and Chirp parity sources of truth rather than creating parallel planning state.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p nmp-testing --test doctrine_lint_smoke`

# Title Component: Add Subtitle Line and Character Counts

This PR was made using Fei! Visit [the task in Studio](http://localhost:5173/projects/aeef5ae3-7dce-465a-bdd3-9c9ef519c799/tasks/ed3ca778-bf2b-4d75-abeb-02cea8e09737?version=4) to see this PR working.

---

## Summary
Adds a second editable line (subtitle) to the existing Title component and improves UX around character counts and validation. The change introduces per-line character counts shown while focused, a shared error state that applies outline styling to both lines when validation fails, and read-only support for both lines. All existing functionality is preserved and new props are optional with sensible defaults.

---

## Key Changes
- Added a secondary subtitle input alongside the main title to support two-line titles.
- Added per-field character count indicator shown while the field is focused (80-character default limit, configurable).
- Introduced a shared error outline style so both lines show the same error styling when validation fails.
- Added read-only support and preserved existing readonly behavior for the title; subtitle follows the same rules.
- Preserved existing props and behavior; new props (initSubtitle, maxLengthSubtitle, subtitlePlaceholder) are optional with sensible defaults.
- Cleaned up focus/blur handling and removed stray console.log.

---

## Files Changed
- `src/app/components/title/title.tsx`
  - Added a second TextareaAutosize instance to render a subtitle beneath the main title (flex column layout).
  - Introduced local state for subtitle (initSubtitle prop + setSubtitle) and updateSubtitle handler with max-length enforcement.
  - Added a reusable CharacterCount subcomponent to display current / max character counts when focused.
  - Added ERROR_OUTLINE_CLASSES constant to centralize the error outline classes and applied it to both title and subtitle.
  - Adjusted focus handling: onFocus enables character count display, onBlur hides it (removed a stray console.log).
  - Applied typography classes: title uses font-primary-black text-2xl, subtitle uses font-primary-regular text-base.
  - Added autofocus to the main title TextareaAutosize to preserve previous behavior.
  - Extended TitleProps with optional initSubtitle, maxLengthSubtitle, and subtitlePlaceholder props; defaults provided.

---

## Implementation Notes
- CharacterCount: a small presentational component that renders `current / max` only while the field is focused; turns red when the limit is reached.
- Shared error styling: ERROR_OUTLINE_CLASSES centralizes error-outline classes and is applied to both TextareaAutosize instances when the `error` prop is present and validation fails.
- Validation: existing validation for title (empty or only-spaces) remains; when validation fails, the same error string is shown and both inputs receive error outline styling.
- Props and defaults:
  - initSubtitle: optional initial subtitle value (default: "").
  - maxLengthSubtitle: optional max length for subtitle (default: 80).
  - subtitlePlaceholder: optional placeholder for subtitle (default: "Write the subtitle").
- Layout: container changed to a vertical stack (flex column) with a small gap to visually separate title and subtitle.
- Dependencies: continues to use the existing TextareaAutosize component and utility textAreOnlySpaces. No new external libraries introduced.
- Accessibility: character count is visually shown while focused. No changes were made to ARIA attributes in this change set; consider adding aria-live updates or aria-describedby for screen reader support in a follow-up if needed.

---

## How to Test
1. Navigate to the page that renders the Title component (where previously the single-line title existed).
2. Verify the main title input renders with bold/large typography (font-primary-black text-2xl) and autofocus is applied.
3. Verify a second subtitle input renders below with regular smaller typography (font-primary-regular text-base).
4. Click into either input and confirm a character count (e.g. "0 / 80") appears below the focused field.
5. Type up to the configured max length for each field and verify:
   - Character count updates live.
   - Additional input beyond the max is prevented.
   - When the limit is reached the count text turns the danger color.
6. Trigger validation error (e.g. clear the title or input only spaces) and confirm:
   - The provided `error` string appears next to the title input.

## Summary

Removes \`AicpuSoInfo\` struct + its runtime H2D allocation of the AICPU SO bytes. The comment claimed this H2D was \"load-bearing on a5 onboard\" — empirically validated as **stale against current HEAD** by experiment PR #875 (a5 onboard CI passed with so_info_.init removed).

Likely cause of the original finding becoming stale: **PR #864** (persistent streams + eager bootstrap) and/or **PR #870** (AICore handle cache stops the 365KB/run ELF leak) removed the implicit HBM-state dependency that earlier reproductions of the 507899 cascade hit.

## What changes

Both archs (a2a3 + a5 onboard):

- Drop \`AicpuSoInfo\` struct + impl, \`so_info_\` member, \`so_info_.init/finalize\` callsites.
- Kept zero-initialized \`DeviceArgs::aicpu_so_bin/len\` fields (offsets 96/104 are still nominally part of libaicpu_extend_kernels' ABI; nothing on our per-task path reads them).

## Net effect

- **-126 LoC** (-174 / +48 across 4 files).
- Saves one ~MB-class memcpy of the AICPU SO bytes per worker init.
- Saves the device-side HBM region that held them.
- ABI / Python surface unchanged.

- \`st-onboard-a2a3\` / \`ut-a2a3\` on #875 failed on the same env flakes seen on #864 / #874: 507018 HCCL cascade and a googletest source download timeout. Unrelated to this change; we expect them green here.

author: terrxo
body:
## Hivemind #266 Phase 1 — gruntcode side

Bridges gruntcode's per-turn lifecycle to the hivemind-mcp loop primitive shipped in hivemind-mcp v0.8.2 ([PR #18](https://github.com/grunt-it/hivemind-mcp/pull/18)) + extended in v0.8.3 ([PR #20 await-review](https://github.com/grunt-it/hivemind-mcp/pull/20)). Every step-finish fires `hivemind_record_turn_end`; every successful tool-result fires `hivemind_loop_progress`. The MCP decides whether to auto-wake the same peer (`continue`), wake the parent (`escalate` / `await-review`), or no-op. **Workers self-drive toward goals WITHOUT Nik typing.**

## Architecture

```
gruntcode tab finishes a step
        ↓
processor.ts case 'step-finish' (after value.reason captured)
        ↓
HivemindLoopHook.recordTurnEnd → MCP.callTool('hivemind_record_turn_end')
        ↓                                  fire-and-forget via Effect.forkIn(scope)
        ↓                                  Effect.ignore swallows any error
hivemind-mcp evaluateLoop decides:
  • continue → wake same peer with continuation prompt
  • escalate → wake parent with violation context (idle-phrase / stalled / recursion)
  • await-review → wake parent (peer signaled 🚦 READY FOR REVIEW)
  • noop → clean exit (done / rate-limited / no goal)

(Independently, every successful tool-result fires hivemind_loop_progress to
keep last_loop_progress_at fresh — cheap signal for the 'silent stall'
detection logic in evaluateLoop.)
```

## Feature flag

**Opt-in per-tab via `OPENCODE_HIVEMIND_LOOP_ENABLED=1`.** Default off in Phase 1; planned default-on in Phase 2 after validating in the wild.

When unset: both hooks are silent no-ops. The processor still yields `MCP.Service` as an Option (`Effect.serviceOption`) but never calls into it.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/opencode/src/session/hivemind-loop-hook.ts` | **NEW.** `HivemindLoopHook.recordTurnEnd` + `HivemindLoopHook.loopProgress`. Both take `Option<MCP.Service>` so tests don't have to provide MCP just to satisfy a single-hook env requirement. `findHivemindClient` fast-paths the conventional `hivemind` client name; slow-paths a scan of `tools()` by tool-name suffix for users who renamed it. `buildTurnSummary` deferred until AFTER client resolution. |
| `packages/opencode/src/effect/runtime-flags.ts` | New `hivemindLoopEnabled` flag (`OPENCODE_HIVEMIND_LOOP_ENABLED`). |
| `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` | Yield `MCP.Service` via `Effect.serviceOption` (doesn't leak through `Handle.process`'s never-environment signature). `step-finish` case fires `recordTurnEnd`. `tool-result` case fires `loopProgress`. |
| `packages/opencode/test/session/hivemind-loop-hook.test.ts` | **NEW.** 5 tests covering gating paths. |
| `GRUNTCODE.md` | Documented as patch #5. |

## Hard correctness rule: hook MUST NEVER break the TUI

Both hooks pipe through:

```ts
yield * Effect.promise(() => client.callTool(...)).pipe(
  Effect.tapError((err) => Effect.sync(() => log.warn("...", { err }))),
  Effect.ignore,                  // swallow ALL errors
  Effect.forkIn(input.scope),     // never block the caller
)
```

So even if hivemind-mcp is unreachable / slow / errors / panics, the TUI keeps working. The loop primitive's whole point is to PREVENT failures, not cause them.

## Testing

- `bun typecheck` from `packages/opencode`: green.
- `bun test test/session/`: **357 pass / 5 skip / 1 todo / 0 fail** (was 352 pre-hook; +5 new hook tests). No regressions across the session module.

The 5 new tests cover gating paths:
- flag off + MCP=None → silent no-op
- flag on + MCP=None → silent no-op (no error)
- flag off (loopProgress) → silent no-op
- flag on + MCP=None (loopProgress) → silent no-op
- flag on + MCP=Some (stub w/ empty `clients()`) → silent no-op (findHivemindClient miss path)

The wake fire-path is exercised end-to-end by the production loop primitive once Phase 1 is enabled per-tab. That's better validated by live use than by mocked MCP calls in unit tests.

## How to enable per-tab

```sh
# Single tab opt-in:
OPENCODE_HIVEMIND_LOOP_ENABLED=1 gruntcode --peer-id nik-tab-N --project /path/to/repo
```

Or set in shell rc to enable for every gruntcode launch from that shell.

Worker MUST also call `hivemind_set_loop_goal` on takeoff for the loop to drive it (the hook just emits events; the MCP's evaluateLoop noops with a warn if no `loop_goal` is set on the peer). Once #266 Phase 2 lands, takeoff-AGENTS.md will require it.

## Refs

- hivemind #266 (parent — Phase 1)
- hivemind-mcp PR #18 (Phase 0 — schema + 6 tools) — merged 631d234
- hivemind-mcp PR #20 (await-review decision branch) — merged 65a1020
- AGENTS.md + hivemind-peers.md three-layer goal-loop contract (the behavioral rules this PR mechanically enforces)

## Out of scope

- Phase 1.5 (also POST to remote hivemind worker `/orch/tab-turn-end` for the per-tab CoordinatorJob DO) — depends on #268 hivemind worker stand-up first
- Phase 2 (default-on + AGENTS.md TAKEOFF enforcement) — separate PR after this is validated in the wild
- Phase 3 (CoordinatorJob DO class in hivemind worker) — separate program; this PR is purely local-side

🤖 _generated with Claude Code via nik-tab-4 (opencode worker peer)_

## What's broken

From QA console:
```
Loading the script 'https://www.gstatic.com/cv/js/sender/v1/cast_sender.js?loadCastFramework=1'
violates the following Content Security Policy directive:
"script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com".
```

The watch screen ([web/src/routes/watch/\[id\]/+page.svelte:276](web/src/routes/watch/%5Bid%5D/+page.svelte#L276)) injects `cast_sender.js` from gstatic.com when the user opens a video item. CSP blocks the load → SDK silently no-ops → Cast button is dead.

## The fix

[internal/api/middleware/security.go](internal/api/middleware/security.go) — add `https://www.gstatic.com` to:
- `script-src` (for cast_sender.js)
- `frame-src` (for the Cast picker iframe — frame-src has to be set explicitly since `frame-ancestors 'none'` only controls inbound framing, not what we embed)

Added a `TestSecurityHeaders_CSPAllowsGoogleCastSDK` regression next to the existing Cloudflare Insights one.

## Local verification

Built + restarted the dev server. New CSP header:

```
script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com https://www.gstatic.com
frame-src 'self' https://www.gstatic.com
```

```
go test ./internal/api/middleware/ -run 'SecurityHeaders|CSP' -count=1
ok  	github.com/onscreen/onscreen/internal/api/middleware	0.139s
```

## Companion issue from the same QA console: `/watch-status` 404

`GET .../api/v1/items/<id>/watch-status 404` is **not** a code bug. The handler in [internal/api/v1/watch_status.go](internal/api/v1/watch_status.go) already returns `200 + empty status` on `ErrNotFound` (landed via PR #27 / commit 93a5bad). The QA server is running a build that predates that fix — a redeploy from main resolves it. No change needed in this PR; this PR + a fresh deploy clear both console errors.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive analysis documentation for **Task 2.1: Skill Infrastructure** as part of the Package Plugin System (Issue #14). The implementation is ready to begin based on consensus between API and security reviews.

## Analysis Documents

- [API Design](analysis/api-skill-infrastructure.md) - Complete API design for skill infrastructure
- [Security Review](analysis/security-skill-infrastructure.md) - Security analysis and requirements
- [Consensus Summary](analysis/reporting/2.1-skill-infrastructure/consensus.md) - Integrated findings and implementation plan

## Approach

Skills are **context injection modules** that inject guidance into LLM conversations via user-level messages. The infrastructure:

1. **Mirrors AgentDefinition pattern** - Skills are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter
2. **Reuses security controls** - PathGuardrail for directory validation, yaml.safe_load() for safe parsing
3. **Injects via user messages** - No system prompt modification, skills visible but lightweight
4. **Namespace strategy** - `{package}:{skill}` for package skills, plain names for user/project skills

### Key Components

- **Skill dataclass** (frozen, immutable)
- **SkillLoader** - Parse frontmatter, validate fields, load from directories
- **SkillRegistry** - Register, list, lookup skills
- **Context injection** - Inject skill content into user messages

### Security Requirements (MUST Implement)

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| SEC-1 | Use `yaml.safe_load()` for all YAML parsing |
| SEC-2 | Validate skill directories against allowed paths |
| SEC-3 | Enforce skill size limits (100KB max) |
| SEC-4 | Resolve symlinks before validation |
| SEC-5 | Namespace package skills |

### Estimated Time

**2-3 hours** for implementation as specified in TODO.md.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Unit tests for SkillLoader, SkillRegistry, context injection
- [ ] Security tests for path traversal, symlink escape, size limits, YAML safety
- [ ] Integration tests for agent skill loading, CLI commands
- [ ] Test coverage >80% for skills module

## References

body: ## Summary Ships the full `sandbox::*` AI-agent DX work in one commit. Reduces workflow TTHW (time-to-hello-world) from 4 tool calls to 1, returns structured/resubmittable errors from every sandbox function, and wires handler-boundary tracing across all 17 sandbox handlers. ### Highlights - **`sandbox::run`** — meta-function composing `create + fs::write + exec + stop` into a single call. Auto-stops the VM on success/failure unless `keep_sandbox: true`. - **`sandbox::catalog::list`** — new function returning the daemon's image catalog (bundled presets + operator-registered `custom_images`). Closes the "what images exist here" discovery loop. - **Flexible input shapes** - `exec.cmd` accepts `cmd + args`, `argv` array, or shell-line `cmd` (shlex-split). - `exec.env` / `create.env` accept both `Vec<"K=V">` and `{ K: V }` map shapes. - `is_valid_env_name` pins names to `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` (rejects digit-leading / `/`-`-`-`=` with `S001`). - **`fs::read` inline body** — returns UTF-8 string for text under 1 MiB; large/binary still streams via `StreamChannelRef`. - **Structured errors** — every `sandbox::*` returns `{ code, type, message, docs_url, retryable, fix, fix_note }`. `docs_url` anchored at in-repo README (`#S001`, `#S211`, ...). `fix` is a non-null JSON payload the agent can resubmit verbatim when recovery is unambiguous (e.g. `FsParentNotFound` carries `{ "parents": true }`). - **`RunStepFailed`** — when a `sandbox::run` sub-step fails, `inner_code` surfaces transparently and `fix.context` names the failing step plus `fix.sandbox_id` when `keep_sandbox: true`. - **`SandboxErrorWire`** wrapper makes `Display` emit the JSON payload through the `iii_sdk` async handler boundary so envelopes round-trip without per-handler serialization. - **Default exec timeout 30s -> 300s (5m)** — sized for cold `npm install` / `pip install` / `cargo build`. The old 30s default fired as an opaque engine-gate denial before the daemon could return a structured `timed_out:true` response. - **Handler-boundary tracing** — `log_handler_result` emits `tracing::info!` on both success and error with a stable field set (`function_id`, `sandbox_id`, `success`, `error_code`, `error_type`, `retryable`, `duration_ms`). Wired into all 17 sandbox handlers. - **All 10 `sandbox::fs::*` functions** migrated from legacy `RegisterFunctionMessage` to `RegisterFunction::new_async` with full JSON Schema, field docs, and worked examples. `FsEntry`, `FsMatch`, `FsSedFileResult`, `FsReadMeta`, `StreamChannelRef`, `ChannelDirection` all gain `JsonSchema` derives. - **Agent-facing docs** — README gets per-`S`-code anchored subsections (``) plus an Agent Quickstart. `SANDBOX_AGENT_GUIDE` is a paste-into-system-prompt cheat sheet (doctest pins contents against wire format). ### New tests - `sandbox_docs_anchor_stability.rs` — every `SandboxErrorCode` has a README anchor. - `sandbox_fs_decode_error_wire.rs` — decode-error wire shape. - `sandbox_fs_read_buffer_boundary.rs` — byte-loss boundary check for the inline-UTF-8 read fast path. ### Backwards compatibility Wire shape stays additive: missing `argv`/`env` fields default to empty, existing `Vec` env shape still deserializes, error code propagation still works via `map_iii_err`'s three-path matching. Shell worker (`workers/shell`) regression-checked: 20/20 sandbox dispatch tests pass unchanged. ## Test plan - [x] `iii-worker` lib tests pass (770+, incl. 5 new: `catalog::list`, `RunStepFailed` wire shape, `FsParentNotFound` fix payload, handler-boundary trace shape) - [x] `iii-worker` integration tests pass (1228 / 1228, 7 pre-existing ignored) - [x] `workers/shell` sandbox dispatch tests pass (20/20) - [x] Doctest pins `SANDBOX_AGENT_GUIDE` contents against the wire format - [ ] Manual smoke: `sandbox::run` end-to-end with a real workload - [ ] Manual smoke: `sandbox::catalog::list` against a daemon with `custom_images` registered ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added sandbox::run meta-function and sandbox::catalog::list. * Exec/create accept multiple command shapes (cmd+args, argv, shlex'd cmd) and env as vector or map; argv wins when present. * Many sandbox fs endpoints now publish typed request/response schemas with examples, per-call timing/tracing, and better error payloads. * Console trigger config is now optional and trigger summaries include full config payload. * **Breaking Changes** * sandbox::fs::read may include an inline UTF‑8 body for small files (additive). * Default sandbox::exec timeout increased from 30s to 300s. [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/iii-hq/iii/pull/1699?utm_source=github_walkthrough&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=change_stack)

author: rmems
body: ## Summary This PR combines the implementation for three related issues into a single cohesive feature branch: - **#75** — Set up configuration for local LLM SAAQ experimentation - **#76** — Create first local SAAQ experiment path for model onboarding - **#85** — Standardize SAAQ experiment output schema for Surrogate_Viz.jl ingestion ## Changes ### Model Infrastructure - **Moved OLMoE model** to `~/.models/safetensors/allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct/` - **Downloaded official HF config files** (`config.json` + `model.safetensors.index.json`) - **Renamed `OlmoeRouter` → `Router`** across entire codebase ### Safetensors Support - **Added `CheckpointFormat` enum** (`gguf` | `safetensors`) to `ModelConfig` - **Implemented safetensors tensor loading** in `Router` with memory-mapped shard access - **Supports BF16, F16, F32** tensor extraction for routing weights and token embeddings - **Auto-detects format** from file extension (.gguf vs directory) ### Configuration & Documentation - **Updated `.env.example`** with: - `$MODEL_ROOT` / `$CORINTH_MODEL_ROOT` for model path conventions - `SAFETENSORS_LINEUP_CONFIG` for safetensors model lineup - `EMBEDDING_BACKEND` for local embedding backend selection - **Added OLMoE entry** to `configs/safetensors_lineup.template.toml` ### Output Schema Standardization - **Created `src/experiment/schema.rs`** with canonical structs: - `ExperimentManifest` — per-run metadata - `ExperimentSummary` — compact downstream summary - `ExperimentMetrics` — quantitative metrics (weight_mse, router_top1_agreement, compression_estimate, etc.) - `ExperimentBundle` — top-level ingestion structure - **Stripped all heartbeat references** from manifest and metrics - **Updated `saaq_latent_calibration.rs`** to emit standardized `ExperimentManifest`/`ExperimentSummary`/`ExperimentMetrics` ## Validation - ✅ `cargo check --no-default-features` — clean - ✅ `cargo test --no-default-features` — **106 tests pass** - ✅ `cargo check --all-targets` — clean (with CUDA) - ✅ rust-analyzer diagnostics — no real issues (only inactive-code weak warnings) ## Cloud Handoff Updated docs reference **IBM Cloud** and **Oracle Cloud** as next cloud onboarding targets (replacing Vultr HGX A100 references). ## Non-Goals - No cloud provisioning in this PR - No model weights committed - No hardcoded absolute paths in committed code - No changes to SAAQ math or router math --- **Closes:** #75, #76, #85 > [!NOTE] > ### Add safetensors checkpoint support to `Router` and rename `OlmoeRouter` to `Router` > - Renames `OlmoeRouter` to `Router` throughout the codebase and renames `gguf_checkpoint_path` / `GGUF_CHECKPOINT_PATH` to `checkpoint_path` / `CHECKPOINT_PATH` in config structs, env vars, and docs. > - Adds `MappedSafetensorsCheckpoint` in [safetensors.rs](https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/pull/91/files#diff-77454ae492726c9da32a1b80efaa0df893a1e42dac1246128d49eac3679c0ff5) that memory-maps sharded or single-file safetensors directories, parses headers, and exposes `extract_tensor_f32` and `extract_token_embedding`. > - Introduces a `CheckpointBackend` enum so `Router` can back routing at runtime with either a GGUF file or a safetensors directory; GPU synapse paths (Q8_0, Q5_K, Q6_K) return `UnsupportedFormat` for the safetensors backend. > - Adds `safetensors_gate_scores` in [routing.rs](https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/pull/91/files#diff-7c7fb4d9f66d1501fb5324351042a746f967c8b73cff0465510724a02d8dfeec) and `resolve_safetensors_adapter` in [adapter.rs](https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/pull/91/files#diff-1a258a9c4e9a266d1fda17f55ef011613f5cb40a19396bf79177f548359d2a57) to validate routing tensor shape and compute gate scores from safetensors weights. > - Adds a new `experiment` module with `ExperimentManifest`, `ExperimentSummary`, `ExperimentMetrics`, `ExperimentBundle`, and `ExperimentWarning` schema types, re-exported from the crate root; `saaq_latent_calibration` example migrates to these types. > - Adds `configs/safetensors_lineup.template.toml` and `SAFETENSORS_LINEUP_CONFIG` env support so examples can discover safetensors models alongside GGUF lineups. > - Risk: `ModelConfig` field rename from `gguf_checkpoint_path` to `checkpoint_path` is a breaking deserialization change for any persisted configs or external callers. > > > > Macroscope summarized 5774cea. > >

body:
## 요약

`docs/rfc/RFC-0200-time-constants-leaf-library.md` draft 신설. Magic Number Time-literal 회고 §3.1 follow-up.

## 동기

회고 문서가 4 사이트 (out-of-scope) 명시:
- `lib/masc_log/log.ml` (2 sites, `86400.0`)
- `lib/core/safe_ops.ml` (1 site, `3600.0`)
- `lib/briefing_compactors/briefing_compactors.ml` (1 site, `3600.0`)

→ `Masc_time_constants` 가 `masc_config` 에 속해 있어 *cycle 발생* 위험.  RFC-0200 은 그 boundary 영구 해결.

## 핵심 제안

```
(현재)                          (RFC-0200 후)

masc_log                       masc_time_constants  ── (NEW leaf)
   ↑                                   ↑     ↑     ↑     ↑
masc_core                       masc_log  masc_core  masc_config  ...
   ↑                                ↑
masc_config (contains          masc_core
  Masc_time_constants)            ↑
                               masc_config
```

Leaf library 신설 → cycle 발생 0 + 모든 caller 자유 사용.

## 변경

- `docs/rfc/RFC-0200-time-constants-leaf-library.md` 신설 (~120 lines)
- 코드 변경 0

## RFC 내용 구성

1. **Context** — 회고 §3.1 link + 4 미적용 사이트
2. **Dep graph** — 현재 vs 제안 후
3. **Proposal** — `masc_mcp.time_constants` leaf library 신설
4. **Risk table** — Low (wrapped false, module name unchanged)
5. **Migration plan** — 단일 PR 5 step
6. **Alternatives** — (A) masc_log 이동, (B) masc_core sub-module, (C) 그대로 두기
7. **Acceptance criteria** — checklist
8. **Out-of-scope** — minute_int 별도 RFC
9. **Open questions** — library 이름 (`time_constants` vs `time` vs `consts`), `wrapped` 결정

## Workaround Signature Gate

WORKAROUND-WAIVED: RFC draft 신설. 시그니처 3종 비해당:

- ❌ Counter-as-Fix
- ❌ String/substring 분류기
- ❌ N-of-M 패치 — architecture proposal, *반복 비용* > *1회 leaf 신설 비용* 명시

## Related

- 회고 문서: `docs/audit/2026-05-27-magic-number-time-literal-series-retrospective.md` §3.1
- PR #19125 (MERGED) — 회고 문서 초안
- PR #19166 (OPEN) — 회고 문서 §2.5b + Step 8 추가

author: davyprotan
body:
## Summary

- Replaces keytar with Electron `safeStorage` for credential storage. Fixes the v0.9.37 crash where `keytar.node` threw a C++ exception that bypassed JS try/catch and abort()ed the main process.
- Adds `profiles.password_enc BLOB` (DB schema v7). Ciphertext now lives in the DB; the encryption key lives in the OS keychain via `safeStorage`.
- keytar is retained for one release for the keytar→safeStorage migration only, and runs inside an Electron `utilityProcess` so a future keytar abort kills only the helper, not the app.

## Architecture

- `electron/keychain-server.js` — loopback HTTP bridge exposing `/encrypt`, `/decrypt`, and one-shot `/legacy/extract` + `/legacy/forget` endpoints. The Next.js child reaches `safeStorage` (which is main-process only) through this bridge.
- `electron/keytar-helper.js` (new) — utilityProcess script that loads `keytar`. Isolated so a NAPI abort can't take down main.
- `src/lib/keychain.ts` — same public API as before (`setPassword/getPassword/deletePassword/isAvailable`). Stores ciphertext in `password_enc` instead of calling keytar.
- `src/lib/db.ts` — schema v7 adds the column; the deferred post-migration runner now does keytar→safeStorage first, then plaintext→safeStorage, then snapshot scrub.

## Migration behaviour

- Background pass on first boot after upgrade walks every `uses_keychain=1` row, extracts via the utilityProcess, re-encrypts via safeStorage, writes the blob, and deletes the legacy keytar entry.
- If the user connects in the first second after boot before the background pass reaches their row, `getPassword` migrates that single row inline so the connect "just works".
- keytar dep is targeted for removal in v0.9.39 once field telemetry confirms migration completed for the user base.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh install: create a new profile with a password, restart, confirm the password autofills on Connect.
- [ ] Upgrade from v0.9.37 with existing `uses_keychain=1` profiles: confirm `audit_log` contains `profile.password_migrated_to_safestorage` entries and that profiles still connect.
- [ ] Connect to a profile *immediately* after launch (before the background migration runs) — should trigger inline migration and still succeed.
- [ ] Delete a profile — verify `password_enc` is cleared and no orphaned data remains.
- [ ] Edit a profile without re-typing the password — verify the keychain link is preserved (existing v0.9.x bug-fix path).

author: cpvlordelo
body:
The fix uses dict-unpacking to build fresh dicts — the current training_step pattern appends references to the original metadata dicts and mutates them in place, which (A) leaks side effects to subsequent code paths that still hold references to `metadata`, and (b) makes the very last iteration read `metadata[0]["prompt"]` *after* iteration 0 already overwrote it, so the last element of the rolled batch ends up with the wrong prompt.

### Problem (A): 

Not affecting anywhere today since `metadata[i]` is not used downstream inside `training_step`, so even though we are changing it in place, this is not affecting anything in downstream code. In the future, if any code uses `metadata[i]` after the in-place modification is done, they would also receive rolled prompts, which we don't want. The fix will prevent this from happening.

### Problem (B) 

Walkthrough with prompts `[A, B, C, D]` (n=4)
  
  The intended `rolled_metadata` should be `[B, C, D, A]` — each item gets the
  *next* item's prompt, wrapping at the end.

  | iter `i` | reads `metadata[(i+1) % 4]["prompt"]` | writes back to `metadata[i]["prompt"]` | state of `metadata` prompts after this iteration |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 0 | `metadata[1]` → `B` (original) | `metadata[0]` ← `B` | `[B, B, C, D]` |
  | 1 | `metadata[2]` → `C` (original) | `metadata[1]` ← `C` | `[B, C, C, D]` |
  | 2 | `metadata[3]` → `D` (original) | `metadata[2]` ← `D` | `[B, C, D, D]` |
  | 3 | `metadata[0]` → **`B`** ← **already mutated in iter 0!** Should have been `A`. | `metadata[3]` ← `B` | `[B, C, D, B]` |
  
  `rolled_metadata` ends up as `[B, C, D, B]` instead of `[B, C, D, A]` — the
  last element is wrong.

  ### Where the bug lives
  
  For any `n ≥ 2`, only the **last iteration** reads a value that an earlier iteration already overwrote. That's because `(n-1 + 1) % n == 0`, and index 0 is the one iteration 0 wrote to. All earlier reads (`metadata[i+1]` for `i = 0..n-2`) hit indices that haven't been touched yet.

 There's also a degenerate case: with `n = 2 ([A, B])`, iteration 0 sets `metadata[0] ← B`, iteration 1 reads `metadata[0]` (already `B`) and writes `metadata[1] ← B` `→` rolled is `[B, B]`. The "wrong" element is still the last one, but it's a more visible 50%-of-the-batch corruption in that case.

author: copilot
body:
The dashboard was stark black/white with no visual hierarchy, and all historical scans were mixed into a single undifferentiated list. Addresses both: a colorful accessible design system and a 31-day/archive split for report history.

## Design system (`gh-pages/style.css`)

Replaces per-page inline `<style>` blocks with a single shared stylesheet using CSS custom properties.

- **Palette:** deep blue `#1565c0` (primary, 5.9:1 on white) + teal `#00695c` (secondary, 5.6:1) — all pairs pass WCAG 2.2 AA
- **Dark mode:** `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block recalculates every token so contrast holds in both modes
- Colored table `<thead>`, card left-border accents, green/amber violation count badges
- Skip-to-main link, 3px visible focus rings, `scope="col"` on all `<th>`, `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on sections

## 31-day active window

`app.js` and `reports.js` now filter runs client-side:

```js
const cutoff = Date.now() - 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const rows = allRuns.filter(run => {
  if (!run.createdAt) return true; // undated → treat as active
  const ts = new Date(run.createdAt).getTime();
  return Number.isFinite(ts) && ts >= cutoff;
});
```

When older runs exist, a teal banner with count + "View archive" link is injected above the table.

## Archive page (`archive.html` + `archive.js`)

- Merges `history.json` and `report-index.json` by run ID so every archived run has a consistent entry
- Exposes **ZIP download only** — no direct HTML report links for runs > 31 days old
- Sorted newest-first; clearly states users must unzip to access HTML/JSON

## `DESIGN.md`

New repo-root doc following the [STYLES.md](https://github.com/mgifford/STYLES.MD) format — records every token with its contrast ratio, typography rules, accessibility constraints, the 31-day data architecture rationale, and AI agent rules for future edits.

## Summary

Refait propre ce que `fa11154` (set `CI=false`) avait masqué : tous les warnings ESLint sont corrigés (22 sur 7 fichiers) et le garde-fou CI est réactivé.

## Pourquoi

`CI=false` débloque le déploiement à court terme, mais ouvre la porte à des warnings non vus à long terme. Mieux vaut une base propre.

## Catégories de changements

- **Imports morts** : `Camera`, `Eye`, `CheckCircle`, `X`, `AlertCircle`, `LineChart`, `Download`, `compressImage`, `useAuth`, `DBService`, `STORES`…
- **`useState` morts** : `pdfUrl`, `pdfBlob`, `photo`, `file`, `isAdmin`, `workers` — valeurs assignées jamais lues
- **Fonctions mortes** dans `WorkerInterface.js` : `isIOS`, `canDeletePhoto`, `previewPhoto`, `handleTaskCompletion` + le modal `confirm-completion` (seul appelant : `handleTaskCompletion`)
- **`useEffect` mort** dans `SiteManagement.js` qui chargeait des `workers` depuis Supabase pour ne rien en faire
- **Destructures inutiles** : `const { data, error }` → `const { error }` dans 3 endroits où `data` n'était pas utilisé
- **Précédence ambiguë** : `dbService.js` UUID, ajout de parenthèses explicites

- `CI=true` à nouveau actif → tout nouveau warning bloquera le build (effet de cliquet)

author: varashi
body:
## Summary

Add a non-k8s deployment path so homelab users without a Kubernetes cluster can run scaleplex. The same three components (worker, orchestrator, PMS docker-mod) run as plain Docker containers; the PMS docker-mod is unchanged (already shipped at `ghcr.io/varashi/scaleplex_pms_dockermod`).

**Three worker discovery modes now coexist on the orchestrator**, deduped by URL into a single internal pool, removed only when no source vouches:

- **DNS** (existing) — `net.LookupHost(WORKERS_DNS)`; works on k8s headless Services AND docker compose user-defined bridges (compose's embedded DNS returns one A record per replica).
- **LIST** (new) — `WORKERS_LIST=host[:port],...` parsed at startup. Fixed multi-host without DNS infra.
- **PUSH** (new) — worker POSTs `/register` on startup + every `SCALEPLEX_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` (default 5); orchestrator reaps PUSH entries after `WORKERS_PUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 15). Friction-free Docker multi-host: a fresh `docker run` of the worker joins the fleet with one env var.

## Changes

**Orchestrator** (`orchestrator/main.go`):
- `sourceBits` bitset (DNS|LIST|PUSH) on each worker; pool re-keyed by URL so all three sources dedup naturally
- `parseWorkerList` + `pool.loadList` + `pool.register` + `pool.reapPush`
- `POST /register` handler (idempotent — covers initial register and periodic heartbeat in one endpoint)
- `pushReaperLoop` goroutine
- `/workers` JSON gains a `sources` field for observability

**Worker** (`worker/agent/register.go`, new):
- `startRegisterLoop()` — no-op unless `SCALEPLEX_ORCHESTRATOR_URL` is set, so existing k8s/DNS deployments are byte-for-byte unchanged
- `SCALEPLEX_WORKER_HOST` (preferred) or `os.Hostname()` (compose fallback — container name resolves on the user-defined bridge)
- exponential backoff capped at 30s on POST failures
- context-cancellable for clean shutdown

**`deploy/docker/`** (new):
- `compose.yaml` — single-host all-in-one (orchestrator + worker + commented LSIO plex stanza with `DOCKER_MODS` wiring)
- `multi-host.md` — topology diagram, three discovery modes walkthrough, per-host `docker run` recipes, host `perf_event_paranoid` sysctl note, troubleshooting, "what this does NOT cover" callout (WAN, auth, TLS)
- `.env.example` — every knob documented with one-line rationale

**README** — Deploy section restructured into parallel "Kubernetes" and "Docker / docker-compose" sub-sections (k8s narrative preserved verbatim); repo-layout table gains `deploy/docker/`; security posture line up top.

**CI** — `.github/workflows/docker-compose-smoke.yaml` runs `docker compose config` + brings the orchestrator up + POSTs a fake `/register` + verifies the worker shows up in `/workers` with `sources:push`. Worker is skipped (no GPU on GH-hosted runners).

body:
## What

Fix the two **ERROR-level** `auth_users_exposed` advisors flagged by the Supabase email today.

`public.compliance_alerts_view` and `public.reverify_queue_v` both LEFT JOIN `auth.users` to surface user emails next to compliance / background-check status. Both views had **SELECT (and DML)** granted to the `anon` role — meaning anyone with our publishable / anon key could hit them via PostgREST and read user emails.

## Fix

Single migration that:
1. Recreates both views with `security_invoker = true` (enforces querying user's RLS, not creator's)
2. `REVOKE ALL` from `anon`, `authenticated`, `PUBLIC`
3. `GRANT SELECT` only to `service_role`

## Why it's safe

Both views are admin dashboards. Admin code paths already use `createAdminClient()` (service-role key), so no application code change is required. I verified the grants in prod after applying — only `postgres` and `service_role` retain access.

## Already applied

This migration was applied to the production database via the Supabase API immediately after the security email landed, in agreement with the user. **This PR captures the migration in source control** so the Supabase branching workflow stays consistent.

## Files

- `supabase/migrations/20260527_revoke_anon_auth_users_views.sql` (new, 62 lines)

## Advisor impact

| Lint | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `auth_users_exposed` (ERROR) | 2 | **0** |
| `security_definer_view` (ERROR) | 15 | 13 |
| **Total advisors** | 97 | 93 |

Remaining 93 advisors (13 SECURITY DEFINER views, 19 function search_path warnings, 48 anon/authenticated DEFINER function executable flags, storage bucket listing, etc.) will be addressed in follow-up PRs after B7.

## Tests

DDL-only; no test changes. Verified post-apply with:
```sql
SELECT grantee, privilege_type FROM information_schema.role_table_grants
WHERE table_name IN ('reverify_queue_v','compliance_alerts_view');
-- Only postgres and service_role remain.
```

Re-ran `get_advisors` — both `auth_users_exposed` ERRORs cleared.

author: lucvanrhyn
body:
## Summary

Closes #436 (parent PRD #434).

The inline `handleConditionSubmit` in `app/[farmSlug]/logger/[campId]/page.tsx` previously queued the observation, fire-and-forget `syncNow()`, then `router.push(loggerRoot)` — so a 422 `DUPLICATE_OBSERVATION` detected during the background sync went to the dead-letter bucket invisibly. The farmer had already navigated away, so the form closed silently and no UI feedback ever appeared.

This wave performs a synchronous POST to `/api/observations` during the inline submit and runs the response through `classifySyncFailure` (the same single source of truth `lib/sync-manager.ts` uses during the background sync). On 422 DUPLICATE with `existingId` the handler surfaces `resolution.toast.message` as a visible `role="alert"` toast on the page; on 2xx the navigate flow runs unchanged so the happy path shows no regression.

Offline / network-error branches fall through to the existing queue path — the background sync's own classifier (PR #444 / issue #435) auto-resolves the row when connectivity returns. The IDB queue write happens BEFORE the inline POST so a mid-submit network drop can never lose data; the server upsert on `clientLocalId` collapses any retry against the inline POST to a single row.

## Files touched

- `app/[farmSlug]/logger/[campId]/page.tsx` — import `classifySyncFailure` + `SyncToastHint`; add `submitToast` state; do inline POST + classify in `handleConditionSubmit`; render the toast surface at the bottom of the JSX (role=alert)
- `__tests__/logger/camp-condition-duplicate-toast.test.tsx` — NEW unit test (2 cases): asserts the duplicate path renders the classifier-sourced toast, asserts no toast on the happy path
- `e2e/camp-condition-duplicate-toast.spec.ts` — NEW E2E regression spec; double-submits identical Good/Full/Intact then asserts the toast; self-skips when `E2E_IDENTIFIER` / `E2E_PASSWORD` unset

author: andreasalbertqc
body:
# Motivation

The v2.10.0 release wheel build failed on `linux-64` and `linux-aarch64` ([failed run](https://github.com/Quantco/dataframely/actions/runs/26503473342)) while the same SHA's `push`-triggered build on `main` succeeded. On `release` events, `docker-options` expands to `-e CARGO=\${{ env.CARGO }}`, but no host step was setting `CARGO` on Linux — so the value passed to the container was empty, which clobbered `CARGO` inside it and broke `cargo rustc`.

# Changes

Add a Linux-side `Prepare cargo-auditable wrapper` step that sets `CARGO=/usr/local/bin/cargo-auditable-wrapper` — the path of the wrapper that `before-script-linux` already creates inside the manylinux container.

author: ultraub
body:
## Summary
CDS alert acknowledgements were already being persisted to `localStorage` *and* sent to the backend feedback endpoint, but **previously-acknowledged alerts kept re-appearing in the modal on every page view**. Acknowledging a single alert in the open modal made it disappear immediately (the filter worked), but navigating away and back re-popped the same alerts that had already been dismissed.

## Root cause
`CDSPresentation`'s `useState()` lazy initializers for `dismissedAlerts` and `snoozedAlerts` only run on the first render. If `patientId` was `undefined` at that moment (the parent context hadn't resolved the current patient yet), the empty `Set`/`Map` seeded then stuck forever — so the filter that hides dismissed alerts had no entries to match, and every previously-acknowledged alert re-appeared.

Verified live on prod: patient `1126180`'s localStorage held **4 acknowledged alerts** (colonoscopy/mammography/patient-greeter/food-as-medicine-ckd) that were all visible in the modal anyway. Clicking Acknowledge inside the open modal made that alert disappear immediately (4→3), confirming the filter works once state is populated.

## Fix
Add a `useEffect([patientId])` that re-reads `cdsAlertPersistence.getDismissedAlerts(patientId)` and `getSnoozedAlerts(patientId)` whenever `patientId` resolves or changes. The persistence layer was already correct — the bug was purely the component reading from it at the right moment.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open the patient chart; acknowledge an alert in the popup
- [ ] Navigate to another tab and back — the acknowledged alert should not re-appear
- [ ] Reload the page — acknowledged alerts within the 24h TTL should still be hidden
- [ ] Switch to a different patient — alerts are scoped per patient (no leak across patients)

author: evervault-dependencies
body:
Linear: COM-270

## Vulnerability

- **Affected package:** `rust-rustls-webpki` `< 0.103.13` → Fixed in `0.103.13`
- **Severity:** HIGH (CVSS 7.5)
- **SLA deadline:** 2026-06-05T01:44:21.256Z
- **Dependabot alert:** https://github.com/evervault/evervault-cli/security/dependabot/53
- **Advisory:** GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8 — Reachable panic in CRL parsing in `rustls-webpki`. Only reachable when CRL revocation checking is explicitly enabled via `RevocationOptions`; default rustls configurations that do not use CRLs are safe.

## Change

Ran `cargo update` per the standard Rust patching procedure, refreshing the entire workspace lockfile to the latest semver-compatible versions.

## Note on `rustls-webpki` version

The lockfile resolution still pins `rustls-webpki` at `0.101.7`. This is the latest available release in the `0.101.x` line, and it is held there by the transitive constraint chain:

```
rustls-webpki ^0.101.0   (required by)
└── rustls v0.21.12       (required by)
    └── tokio-rustls v0.24.1 (declared in crates/ev-enclave/Cargo.toml as "0.24")
```

The fix in `0.103.13` lives in the `rustls-webpki` `0.103.x` line, which is only pulled in by `rustls` `0.23.x` / `tokio-rustls` `0.26.x`. Advancing the CLI to that line requires a `tokio-rustls` major-version bump (`0.24` → `0.26`) plus matching code updates in `crates/ev-enclave/src/attest/` for the rustls 0.23 API changes (`Certificate` → `CertificateDer`, `ServerName` move to `rustls-pki-types`, new `ServerCertVerifier` method surface, removal of `with_safe_defaults`, etc.). That refactor is outside the scope of a simple dependency bump.

## Reachability

The enclave attestation code uses a custom `ServerCertVerifier` (`SubjectAltNameAttestationValidator`) with an empty `RootCertStore` and does not invoke CRL revocation checking via `RevocationOptions`, so the vulnerable CRL-parsing code path in `rustls-webpki` is not reached at runtime by this CLI.

## Verification

- `cargo update` ran cleanly.
- `cargo check --workspace` builds successfully against the refreshed lockfile.

Wave 4 of the Sprint 3 plan needs Wrkr to treat high-stakes authority as a first-class contract across inventory, risk, graph, and buyer-facing report output. - fail closed for uncorrelated OpenAPI/route production-data surfaces while allowing repo-correlated API authority joins

### containerd user ID handling bypass allows runAsNonRoot evasion
[CVE-2026-46680](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46680) / [GHSA-fqw6-gf59-qr4w](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fqw6-gf59-qr4w) / [GO-2026-5378](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5378)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
A bug was found in containerd where containers launched with a numeric `User` directive that cannot be parsed as a 32-bit integer are incorrectly treated as a username. If a crafted image provides an `/etc/passwd` file mapping this large numeric string to root, the container ultimately runs as root (UID 0). This allows the Kubernetes `runAsNonRoot` restriction to be bypassed, causing unexpected behavior for environments that require containers to run as a non-root user.

##### Patches
This bug has been fixed in the following containerd versions:

* 2.3.1
* 2.2.4
* 2.0.9
* 1.7.32

Note: The containerd 2.1 release has reached its [end of life](https://containerd.io/releases/#current-state-of-containerd-releases) and a fixed version is not provided.

Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue.

##### Workarounds
Ensure that only trusted images are used and that only trusted users have permissions to import images. Alternatively, enforcing a specific numeric `runAsUser` in the Kubernetes Pod `securityContext` overrides the `USER` directive in the image and prevents the bypass. Newer versions of Kubernetes, starting with 1.34, also appear to enforce `runAsNonRoot` properly regardless of this bug.

##### Credits
The containerd project would like to thank Lei Wang (@​ssst0n3) for responsibly disclosing this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://redirect.github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

##### Resources
* https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-265r-hfxg-fhmg (CVE-2024-40635)

##### Impact
A vulnerability in containerd allows a maliciously crafted image to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. This renders the container runtime API unavailable and can disrupt clients such as the Docker Engine or Kubernetes control-plane components.

This bug has been fixed in the following containerd versions:

* 2.3.2

* 2.1.9
* 2.0.10
* 1.7.33

##### Workarounds
Ensure that only trusted images are used and that only trusted users have permissions to import images or schedule pods.

- Expands `_DEFAULT_RETRY_ON_EXCEPTIONS` from `{UiPathRateLimitError, UiPathTooManyRequestsError}` (HTTP 429, 529) to also include 408, 502, 503, 504. Applies to every provider client because they all share the same `UiPathHttpxClient` retry transport.

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

Two improvements to the Program Admin Report walkthrough pipeline:

1. The manager-flow recorder now drives the "Initiate AI Assistant" modal end-to-end (open modal → pre-filled prompt → select synthetic bot → edit prompt → click Initiate → conversation appears).
2. A new post-processor compresses every "loading screen" run in a recorded video down to ~1 second each. A 14-minute drill-through recording that's mostly stuck waiting on GDrive image streaming becomes a 30-second one. A 57-second manager flow with auth gates becomes 13 seconds.

End-to-end: the final combined PAR walkthrough video is now **1:20** (was 14:20 with the same content).

## Technical Summary

### `record_manager_flow.py` updates
- Scene 1 matches the post-#272 UI: button text "Mark all non-flagged FLWs as No Issue" + assert ≥9 "No Issues" pills (was "Confirmed No Issue").
- Scene 5 directly navigates to /tasks/<id>/edit/ after Create Task with Coaching (the chc_nutrition button now does the navigate itself; the old View Task hop is gone).
- Scenes 6-8 are new: open Initiate AI modal, wait for prompt pre-fill + synthetic bot in dropdown, type a small prompt edit (visual beat), click inner "Initiate AI" (selector scoped via exact text match), wait for "Coaching Conversation" block.

### `scripts/walkthroughs/_lib/compress_loading.py`
Perceptual-hash-based loading-screen detector + compressor:
- Sample input at 5fps, compute a 16x16 luminance hash per frame.
- Consecutive frames with hash distance under `IDENTITY_THRESHOLD` (default 1200) are treated as the same "scene".
- Static runs longer than `max_static_seconds` (default 1.0) get truncated to that duration; everything else passes through.
- Animated spinners stay classified as "static" because the global frame hash barely moves with local rotation.

CLI: `python -m scripts.walkthroughs._lib.compress_loading INPUT.mp4 --out OUTPUT.mp4 --max-static 1.0`

### `.gitignore`
- `scripts/walkthroughs/*/.run_ids.json` — per-run handoff from regenerate.py to recorders, regenerated every session.
- `scripts/walkthroughs/**/__pycache__/`, `scripts/walkthroughs/**/video/`, `video_manager/` — local cruft.

## Safety Assurance

- compress_loading: idempotent — re-running on an already-compressed video is a no-op (re-encoded but no segments dropped, because there are no static runs above the threshold).
- Recorder Scene 8: uses an exact-text match (\`b.innerText.trim() === 'Initiate AI'\`) to disambiguate from the outer "Initiate AI Assistant" button. Tested live; modal closes + page reloads + conversation renders.
- No behavior change for any non-walkthrough flow; all changes are in `scripts/walkthroughs/`.

author: yschimke
body:
The plugin's `onVariants` callback required strict equality against
`extension.variant` (default `"debug"`), so flavored application
modules with `demoDebug`/`prodDebug` and no plain `debug` variant got
zero `composePreview*` tasks registered and were invisible to module
discovery. Closes #1546.

Two changes:

- `AndroidPreviewSupport.variantMatchesTarget` accepts an exact match
  OR a build-type suffix match (target `debug` also matches `demoDebug`,
  `prodDebug`, `uatDebug`). Explicit flavor pins like
  `--variant prodDebug` still match only exactly. When the suffix rule
  fires, the extension's variant Property snaps to the resolved name so
  downstream readers (DiscoverPreviewsTask, model builder, doctor)
  report the real variant.
- `ComposePreviewPlugin` overrides `extension.variant.convention` to
  read the `composePreview.variant` Gradle property, and the CLI gains
  a `--variant <name>` flag that forwards as
  `-PcomposePreview.variant=<name>` on the connection's extraArguments
  (so model queries see it too — without that, flavored apps would
  still be invisible to `findPreviewModules()`).

body:
Phase 3 of the unified version-family work, stacked on #447. Closes #69 along the way.

## Summary

Three vertically-aligned slices, all driven by PRD #442:

1. **Role-aware visibility ranking** — new `src/common/version_visibility.py` module with elevated vs consumer status rank tables and a `collapse_by_family` helper. Wired into the contracts and products list managers, so the family representative is now picked according to caller role:
   * Consumer: `ACTIVE > DEPRECATED` (drafts hidden entirely)
   * Owner / team member / subscriber / admin: `DRAFT > PROPOSED > UNDER_REVIEW > APPROVED > ACTIVE > DEPRECATED`
   Subscription-based elevation is wired in for products via the existing `DataProductSubscriptionDb` table; contracts use ownership-only elevation (no contract subscription table exists today).

2. **Family-latest resolver endpoints** — `GET /api/data-contracts/families/{family_id}/latest` and the products counterpart. These resolve a family-follow-latest reference to a concrete row using the same role-aware rank, so any caller storing only a family id can read back the right version.

3. **EntityVersionPicker** — new shared component in `components/common/entity-version-picker.tsx`. Combobox over the collapsed list endpoint (one row per family, inline version badges), optional Entity-pinned / Family-follow-latest scope toggle, and an inline sub-picker for refining the version when pinning. The `link-contract-to-port-dialog` is migrated as the first call site (closes #69) with \`allowedScopes=['entity']\` until the output-port reference-storage slice lands.

## Closes
- #69 — same-named contracts in the link-contract-to-port dialog now show their version inline, so producers can disambiguate before linking.

## Stacked on
- #447 (list-view collapse + version-count badge)
- #446 (foundation: version_family_id column, migrations, cloning, detail-view UI)

## Test plan
- [x] \`pytest src/tests/unit/test_version_visibility.py\` — 12 cases covering status visibility, rank ordering, tie-breaks, and the consumer-only / admin-only edges. All pass.
- [x] \`pytest src/tests/unit/test_version_family.py\` — added 2 manager-level cases (consumer sees active rep; team member sees in-flight draft rep). All 17 pass.
- [ ] Manual: migrate \`link-contract-to-port-dialog\` flow — verify the picker shows version badges, that selecting a version pins the right contract id, and that the "Create New Contract" inline path still works.

body:
# Pull Request Template

## 📝 Description
Fixes Vercel build failure: `Command "npm run build" exited with 1`

The root cause is that Next.js tries to statically render API routes during build, but all routes use `request.headers` (either directly or through auth middleware/rate limiting). This causes the error:
```
Dynamic server usage: Route /api/... couldn't be rendered statically because it used `request.headers`
```

**Fix:** Added `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` to all 69 API route files, telling Next.js to always render them server-side at request time.

**Verified:** `npm run build` passes successfully after this change.

## 🎯 Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

## 📋 Pre-Submission Checklist

### Code Quality
- [x] Code follows existing style and conventions
- [x] No console.log() statements left in
- [x] No hardcoded secrets or sensitive data
- [x] No unnecessary dependencies added

## 📊 What Changed

### Modified Files
- [x] All 69 files in `/src/app/api/` — Added `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`

### Before/After
**Before:**
```javascript
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import admin from 'firebase-admin';
// ... route handler that uses request.headers
```

**After:**
```javascript
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import admin from 'firebase-admin';
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
// ... route handler that uses request.headers
```

## 🔐 Security Considerations
- [x] No security impact — this is a Next.js rendering configuration, not a logic change

## 🧪 Testing Notes
- [x] `npm run build` completes successfully (was failing before)

author: mammalwithashell
body:
## Summary

Adds a faithfulness-oracle pipeline for the Rust engine: a modded DCGO client that records every player decision as JSONL encoded in our 2192-action space, and a Rust harness (`dcgo-replay`) that replays those recordings through `digimon-engine` to assert parity card-by-card. Also extends the engine with an **opaque-opponent-deck mode** so PvP recordings (where the local client never observes the authoritative opponent shuffle) can replay end-to-end.

OpenSpec change: `openspec/changes/add-dcgo-recording-parity-harness/`
Schema reference: `docs/DCGO_RECORDING_SCHEMA.md`
Build instructions: `docs/DCGO_BUILD.md`

## What's in this PR

Five commits, scoped intentionally:

| Commit | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `362da555` | Bump DCGO submodule to local `add-recording-mod` branch |
| `edb1c22d` | Repoint DCGO submodule URL at our fork |
| `8d30a05b` | Opaque-deck engine mode + action-space codegen pipeline |
| `6bce4eed` | `dcgo-replay` harness — replay DCGO recordings through `digimon-engine` |
| `71041973` | Documentation + OpenSpec change + CLAUDE.md maintenance rule |

### Opaque-deck engine mode

New module `code/digimon-engine/src/opaque_deck.rs` with `RevealKind` enum, `RevealSource` trait, `RevealQueue` concrete impl, and `OpaqueDeckState`. New `Game::new_with_opaque_opponent` constructor; per-player `opaque_deck_state` field. All core deck/security paths wired for opaque mode: initial-hand draw, mulligan redraw (with restore-to-multiset), per-turn draw, lazy security setup (placeholders materialize on flip), 11 effect-driven security access sites, the digivolve-bonus draw, mill, peek, generic `CardSourceRef::DeckTop`/`Security` consumers, and the `<Training>` keyword.

Helpers to use for new opaque-aware code:
- `Game::draw_one_for_player(pid)`
- `Game::take_from_deck_top_for_player(pid, kind)`
- `Game::setup_security_for_player(pid, count)`
- `Game::ensure_security_materialized(pid, idx)`

### Action-space codegen pipeline

New Cargo workspace member `code/tools/action-space-export/`: imports `digimon_engine::action::space::*` and emits a JSON descriptor of all 2192 action IDs. A Python emitter (`emit_csharp.py`) generates `DCGO/Assets/Scripts/Script/Recording/ActionSpace.cs` so the C# recorder encodes decisions in lockstep with the Rust enum. CI gate at `.github/workflows/action-space-codegen-drift.yml` catches drift.

### dcgo-replay harness

New Cargo workspace member `code/tools/dcgo-replay/`. Parses JSONL recordings, dispatches to standard or opaque-deck construction based on `opp_deck_post_shuffle`, asserts mask legality at every step, surfaces failures as `IllegalAction` / `ActorMismatch` / `WinnerMismatch` / `EngineError` / `OpaqueRevealError`. Aggregates over a corpus into a deterministic per-card parity report (BTreeMap-keyed, sorted lists — same corpus = byte-identical JSON output).

### DCGO submodule

Submodule URL repointed from `DCGO2/DCGO` to `mammalwithashell/DCGO` (our fork). The `add-recording-mod` branch lives at `mammalwithashell/DCGO@f1ef41512` with:
- New `Assets/Scripts/Script/Recording/` tree (GameRecorder, ActionEncoder, RecorderConfig, generated ActionSpace.cs, EditMode tests)
- Minimal one-line hooks added to `TurnStateMachine.cs`, `UserSelectionManager.cs`, `CardController.cs` at the 8 chokepoints that capture every decision + every opponent reveal

`git submodule update --init --recursive DCGO` against this branch fetches our fork and resolves the recording-mod SHA cleanly.

## Tests

```
cargo test -p action-space-export                     →   8/8 pass
cargo test -p dcgo-replay                             →  21/21 pass (15 unit + 6 integration)
cargo test --manifest-path code/digimon-engine/...    →  712 pass + 1 pre-existing unrelated fail
cargo test --test opaque_deck                         →  15/15 pass
```

The pre-existing failure (`select_materials::select_materials_batch_play_from_materials_plays_every_picked_source`) was verified independent of this branch — fails on un-modified `origin/main` too.

The most important integration test is `integration_opaque_pvp_recording_passes` in `code/tools/dcgo-replay/tests/integration.rs`: it builds a synthetic PvP recording (5 draw reveals + 5 security reveals + mulligan keep × 2 + concede) and runs it through `Game::new_with_opaque_opponent`. Confirms the harness drives the real Rust engine end-to-end for opaque-mode replays.

## Branch base

Branched off `010e9cdc` (DNA Omnimon EoT chain merge); `origin/main` has 18 newer commits at PR time. The 5 commits here apply cleanly on top — but you may want to rebase before merging to get a linear history.

## What's deferred (not blocking)

These items are tracked as open in `tasks.md` and are out of scope for this PR:

- **Per-prompt selection encoding** (task 3.5): the C# `ActionEncoder.EncodeSelectionInt/Bool` currently emits `encoder_failure` sentinel rows because resolving which `Select*Effect` is prompting requires plumbing identity through 15 selection-class signatures. Replays halt cleanly with `PartialPass` when they hit one of these.
- **DCGO build smoke tests** (1.1–1.3, 3.12, 7.4, 10.5): require local Unity 2021.3.45f2 install + DCGO asset bundle.
- **Bot-fuzzer corpus** (Group 5): blocked on DCGO build above.
- **BC dataset emitter** (Group 9): planned follow-up, depends on real PvP recordings.

OpenSpec change is `--strict` valid at 52/69 tasks complete.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p action-space-export -p dcgo-replay` passes in CI
- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path code/digimon-engine/Cargo.toml --test opaque_deck` passes in CI
- [ ] CI's new `action-space-codegen-drift` workflow runs (warn-only initially per design)
- [ ] Reviewers verify the DCGO C# patches at the chokepoints (TurnStateMachine.cs, UserSelectionManager.cs, CardController.cs) are minimal one-liners and don't change game behavior — the diff is intentionally surgical so it can be rebased onto upstream DCGO updates cheaply
- [ ] Spot-check `docs/DCGO_RECORDING_SCHEMA.md` against `code/tools/dcgo-replay/src/recording.rs` for any spec/impl drift
- [ ] *(if Unity available)* Build DCGO from the `add-recording-mod` branch and run one bot match end-to-end — confirm a JSONL file appears under `Application.persistentDataPath/dcgo_recordings/` and parses with `cargo run -p dcgo-replay -- --input <file>`

author: dudarenok-maker
body:
## Summary

Durable fix for the "two Sophies" duplicate rows in the **Rebaseline the series** modal (plan 122 — follows the data-only cleanup of the live KOTLC workspace). Root cause: the modal and the series-override write both keyed on `voiceId ?? id`, so a recurring character detected under a divergent id that never received a shared `voiceId` split into its own row — and in-book merge / `cast-link-prior` only ever wrote aliases, never the `voiceId`, so they never unified the key. Separately, a real character could end up wearing an `unknown-male`/`unknown-female` id and masquerade as a named bucket.

This collapses recurring cast by name/alias and keeps the approve write honest, with prevention at the two source seams. User-chosen scope: auto-collapse (respecting `notLinkedTo`), full root-cause fix.

What changed (user/dev-visible deltas):

- **`sameCharacterByNameAlias`** (`src/lib/cross-book-duplicates.ts`): normalised name/alias token match reusing `normaliseDuplicateToken` + `looksLikeSameName`; returns false when either side marks the other `notLinkedTo` (the plan-101 "intentionally different" escape hatch) and never matches a fold bucket.
- **`mergeSeriesCast`** now unions series-mates by `voiceId ?? id` AND by name/alias, so divergent-id duplicates ("Sophie"/"Sophie Foster", "Bronte"/"bron-te") collapse to one row with summed lines and the group's designed Qwen voice carried onto the representative. Anchor identity wins.
- **New contract — `POST /api/books/:bookId/cast/:characterId/voice-override-linked`**: the keystone. Rediscovers the same name/alias group across the series (reusing `cast-series-patch`'s matching), unifies their `voiceId` to one canonical key, and writes the Qwen override to every member book — so approving a collapsed modal row reaches books on a divergent key, not just those already sharing `voiceId`. `runApprove` calls it instead of the plain series override; the old voiceId-keyed propagation is preserved as a superset.
- **Prevention:** `cast-link-prior` now also stamps `source.voiceId = target.voiceId ?? target.id` (a manual continuity link truly unifies the propagation key, not just aliases); `fold-minor-cast` canonicalises any bucket-id row back to the generic `Unknown male`/`Unknown female` name on output, so a named character never wears a fold-bucket id (the drifted name is deliberately NOT kept as an alias, so the matcher won't re-bind that character to the bucket).

Behaviour notes: matching stays conservative (exact / strict-substring / punctuation-normalised) — typo-only id variants with no shared token (`aldan` vs `alden`) do NOT auto-collapse, by design; `notLinkedTo` remains the un-merge escape hatch. Propagating a new Qwen voice to a book whose audio is already rendered marks it stale — the explicit intent of a series rebaseline (drift flags the affected chapters). No schema change; existing confirmed books were already repaired by the data fix, this is forward-looking + heals the modal display/propagation.

## Test plan

- **Unit:** `cross-book-duplicates.test.ts` (matcher: substring, alias bridge, normalised-equality, notLinkedTo, bucket guard); `merge-series-cast.test.ts` (name/alias collapse, line-sum, notLinkedTo blocks, Qwen carry, never collapses a bucket).
- **Component:** `rebaseline-modal.test.tsx` — a divergent-id same-name sibling renders ONE row; a `notLinkedTo` sibling stays a SECOND row; approve calls `setVoiceOverrideLinked(homeBookId, characterId, {engine,name})`.
- **Server:** new `voice-override-linked.test.ts` (unify voiceId + propagate across the name/alias group, respect notLinkedTo, preserve voiceId-key propagation, series boundary, standalone, null-clear, 400/404); `cast-link-prior.test.ts` (voiceId unified + id fallback); `fold-minor-cast.test.ts` (drifted bucket canonicalised, no named ≥minLines char on a bucket id).
- **E2E:** existing `e2e/rebaseline.spec.ts` drives open → propose → approve → toast through the new linked-override path (the mock workspace is single-book, so multi-book collapse is covered at the component level).
- `npm run verify` green locally (typecheck + all tests + e2e + visual baselines + build), no flake.

Regression plan: `docs/features/122-rebaseline-name-alias-collapse.md` (+ INDEX entry).

author: mjinah3369
body:
## Why this PR exists

After Step 9 fixed the obvious Card A/B confusion, I ran a systematic audit to surface other places where the dashboard could silently show wrong data at session boundaries (pre-market, RTH, after-hours, settlement, weekends, holidays).

Five categories of real defects fixed below. Several "audit findings" turned out to be hallucinations and were disproved without action.

## What was wrong

### 1. `services/yahooFinance.js` — silent 0% bug (10 call sites)

Every fetcher (futures, currencies, sector ETFs, mag7, treasuries, crypto) used:

```js
const prevClose = meta.chartPreviousClose || price;
```

When Yahoo returned `null` for `chartPreviousClose`, the fallback set prevClose = current price → `change = 0` → `changePercent = 0.00%`. The dashboard displayed a fake "0.00%" instead of "data unavailable." This is the silent failure mode that hid the Card A/B confusion for so long.

**Fix:** new `resolvePrevClose()` helper that:
- Returns null for change/changePercent when previousClose is missing.
- **Clamps implausible moves** at 15% — catches the real-world QQQ bug from yesterday where Yahoo returned previousClose=$609 against price=$730 (19.87% implied move).
- Logs a warning so we can monitor when Yahoo's data goes weird.

All return statements now emit null instead of crashing on `.toFixed()`.

### 2. `services/esCommandCenter.js:46`

Same `chartPreviousClose ||` pattern, same 15% clamp applied.

### 3. `services/dashboardBuilder.js:465,474` — UTC vs ET

Trading notes used `new Date().getHours()` and `.getDay()`. On Render (UTC clock), this is 4-5 hours ahead of ET:

- "Pre-market session" note (hour < 10) fired at 5 AM ET, missed the actual 8-9:30 AM ET window
- "Late session" (hour >= 15) fired at 11 AM ET, missed 3-4 PM ET
- Friday/Monday detection was off-by-one between 8 PM ET and midnight ET

**Fix:** read hour and weekday via `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: 'America/New_York', ... })`.

### 4. `services/fundamentalReports.js` — UTC vs ET on the calendar

`isToday()` / `isTomorrow()` used UTC `getDate()`. Between 8 PM ET (00 UTC) and midnight ET (04 UTC), the Earnings/Fundamental Reports calendar mislabeled tomorrow as "Today." The "past 5 PM, get next week" rollover at line 375 used UTC hours, firing at 1 PM ET (four hours too early).

**Fix:** added `etDateKey()` and `etHour()` helpers; all date comparisons now in ET.

### 5. `server.js:1658` — bogus pivots when previousClose missing

Pivot calculation fell back to `currentPrice` when `previousClose` was null. With prevClose == price, the classic pivot formula collapses R1/R2/S1/S2 onto a single number near the current price — the dashboard would display "support" and "resistance" right on top of where price is now. Useless and misleading.

**Fix:** return null prevClose so the existing `if (pdh && pdl && prevClose)` guard skips pivots cleanly.

## What was NOT changed (audit hallucinations)

The audit agent claimed bugs that I read in full and disproved:

- `sessionEngine.js` timezone — the code already converts to ET (line 100)
- `aiAgents.js` cache TTL bucket — cache key includes session, so safe across boundaries
- `aiAgents.js` Promise.race 15s timeout — not actually a race condition
- `technicalAnalysis.js` forming-candle indexing — correctly handles today-bar-present in else-if branch
- `aiAgents.js` prewarm session race — sessionInfo captured at call time, not stale

## What this does NOT change

- The `aiSynthesis` cache, the synthesis prompt, the pre-warm scheduler — all from Step 9.
- The 8 ETF snapshot pipeline — already correct from Step 9 (uses daily candles, ignores meta.previousClose).
- The Session Brief (uses its own input shape, not affected).
- Any frontend wiring — but **frontend should gracefully handle null** for `change` / `changePercent` / `previousClose`. If a tile renders `.toFixed(2)` on null, it crashes. The number of tiles that hit a null is small (only when Yahoo's data is genuinely broken), but defensive rendering with `value?.toFixed(2) ?? '—'` is correct.

## Test plan
- [ ] Render redeploys
- [ ] `/api/dashboard` and `/api/final-analysis` continue to return 200
- [ ] Snapshot tiles and gainers/losers grids still show real percent values during RTH
- [ ] During pre-market / weekend / holiday, tiles show "—" instead of fake "0.00%" when Yahoo returns null previousClose
- [ ] Earnings/Fundamental Reports calendar correctly labels "Today" and "Tomorrow" past 8 PM ET on Render
- [ ] `tradingNotes` array has "Pre-market" note at 8-9:30 AM ET and "Late session" note at 3-4 PM ET (not 5 AM / 11 AM)
- [ ] No crash in server logs after deploy

## Summary

Adds `ServiceAccount` — machine-to-machine authentication with client ID + secret pairs. Raw secrets never persisted (SHA-256 hash stored).

## Class

`class/xion/ServiceAccount.php`

- `create(name, scopes=[])` — issue `[clientId, rawSecret]`; secret hashed at rest
- `verify(clientId, rawSecret)` — validate credentials; null if wrong/disabled
- `rotate(clientId)` — replace secret; old secret immediately invalid; new raw returned
- `enable/disable(clientId)` — toggle active state
- `find(clientId)` — fetch account record (secret not exposed)
- `all()` — list all accounts
- `delete(clientId)` — permanently remove

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE service_accounts (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    client_id   VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    secret_hash VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    name        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    scopes      TEXT         NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    enabled     TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    created_at  DATETIME     NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    rotated_at  DATETIME     NULL
);
```

author: michaeltrefry
body:
## Summary
Extends the LoRA family detector (`crates/sceneworks-core/src/lora_family.rs`) so bring-your-own Wan LoRAs in **ComfyUI/native** and **Kohya/musubi-tuner** key layouts auto-detect as `wan-video`, instead of scoring 0 and importing with no family.

Previously only diffusers-style `transformer.blocks.` keys were recognized. A LoRA that detected nothing imported as generically "compatible" (empty family matches every model) and silently skipped the `wan-video` base-model gate, forcing users to set the family by hand.

Adds two sibling `Bucket::WanVideo` `BucketSignature`s:
- **ComfyUI / native:** require `diffusion_model.blocks.` + a `self_attn`/`cross_attn`/`ffn` marker. Disqualifies `double_blocks.` / `transformer*_blocks.` so it can't catch ComfyUI Flux/LTX.
- **Kohya / musubi-tuner:** require `lora_unet_blocks_` + `_self_attn_`/`_cross_attn_`/`_ffn_`. Disqualifies the SD/SDXL text-encoder prefixes (`lora_te_`/`lora_te1_`/`lora_te2_`) so a Wan `lora_unet_` LoRA never collides with the Sd15/Sdxl signatures (whose text-encoder keys also contain `_self_attn_`). `lora_unet_blocks_` is itself Wan-specific — SD/SDXL UNet keys are `lora_unet_down_blocks_`/`lora_unet_up_blocks_`/`lora_unet_mid_block_`.

The three Wan prefixes are mutually exclusive, so only one Wan signature scores per file — no within-bucket runner-up-margin contention.

> Note: implemented against the documented community conventions (per the story's key-layout examples), not verified against real sample `.safetensors` files — none were available in this environment. Worth a spot-check against an actual ComfyUI/Kohya Wan LoRA before close.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p sceneworks-core lora_family` — 31 pass (2 new: `detects_comfyui_native_wan_video`, `detects_kohya_wan_video`)
- [x] Full crate suite — 65 unit + integration tests pass, no regressions in SD1.5/SDXL/Flux/LTX/Qwen/Z-Image detection
