author: zzstoatzz
body:
Follow-up to #20699. The per-schedule deployment-selection query filters on `auto_scheduled.is_(True)`, but the partial index that PR added for it — `ix_flow_run__schedule_id_scheduler` — has predicate `auto_scheduled = true`. `IS true` doesn't match `= true` for either planner's predicate-implication prover, so **the index has never been used**; the query has been silently riding the older 2022 index with a post-filter. Switching to `== sa.true()` emits the equality form and activates the purpose-built index on both databases.

<details>
<summary>Empirical proof (~15× faster, ~10× less I/O)</summary>

Throwaway Postgres 16, both production indexes present, 2.2M flow_runs (355 MB), 100 deployments × 20 active schedules × 100 future runs each (the steady-state case where `EXISTS` must evaluate every schedule). Identical query, only `auto_scheduled IS true` → `auto_scheduled = true`:

| | execution time | buffers touched |
|---|---|---|
| current (`IS true`) | ~1,550 ms | 4,041,082 |
| this PR (`= true`) | ~100 ms | 416,068 |

Stable across 3 runs.

**Current** — subquery falls back to the 2022 index and reads *all* of a deployment's scheduled rows, then discards the other schedules':
```
Bitmap Heap Scan on flow_run  (... ix_flow_run__scheduler_deployment_id_auto_scheduled_next_schedu)
  Filter: ((auto_scheduled IS TRUE) AND ((created_by ->> 'id') = ...))
  Rows Removed by Filter: 1900     ← every loop, 2000 loops
  Heap Blocks: exact=4000000
```
The #20699 index is never mentioned.

**This PR** — both subqueries use the #20699 index with the schedule id promoted into the index condition (zero filter waste):
```
Index Scan using ix_flow_run__schedule_id_scheduler on flow_run
  Index Cond: (deployment_id = ... AND (created_by ->> 'id') = ... AND next_scheduled_start_time >= now())
```

The benefit scales with schedules-per-deployment (the old path re-reads a deployment's full scheduled set once *per schedule* — quadratic in schedules/deployment). Single-schedule deployments see no change; high-frequency / multi-schedule setups (cf. #18861) see the most.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why `IS true` vs `= true` matters for partial indexes</summary>

For a regular indexed *column*, Postgres normalizes `IS true` to `= true` as an index condition (which is why the older index, where `auto_scheduled` is a column, kept working for ~2 years). But when `auto_scheduled = true` lives in a *partial index predicate*, the planner must prove the query's predicate **implies** the index predicate, and its implication prover does not treat the `BooleanTest` `IS true` as implying the `OpExpr` `= true`. So the partial index is disqualified. Same on SQLite (`IS 1` vs `= 1`).

Regression test asserts the compiled SQL emits `auto_scheduled = true` / `= 1` (and not `IS true` / `IS 1`) on both dialects — deterministic, unlike an EXPLAIN-based assertion which is meaningless on tiny test tables.

</details>

author: yusufizzetmurat
body:
Closes #307.

Three strict-prior macro-regime indicators per event ride behind a new \`--use-regime-conditioning\` flag on \`app.train_forecaster\`, and a multiplicative gate on \`ForecasterBase\` lets the model modulate the legacy rich-feature slice by the active regime. Default off keeps the per-bar feature size byte-identical to pre-#307 and the gate's zero-init makes the flag-on forward pass identical to the no-gate path at step zero, so the only thing the model learns is whether the conditioning earns its complexity on this corpus. The methodology contribution is the architectural mechanism for handling regime heterogeneity; the headline cell against the flag is a Runpod hand-off, framed honestly per the #334 substitution finding.

- \`policy_cycle_phase_score\` reads \`ff_target_prior\` from strictly-prior MP-surprise rows over the trailing 12 months with ±25 bp thresholds (hiking / cutting / holding).
- \`vix_level_regime_score\` buckets the T-1 VIX against tertiles of the supervised sequence's own prior-bar VIX series.
- \`term_spread_sign\` is the sign of \`tnx_close - irx_close\` at T-1.
- Gate is \`nn.Linear(3, RICH_FEATURE_SIZE - FEATURE_SIZE)\` with zero-init weight + bias and \`2 * sigmoid(...)\` squashing; mounted only when the flag is on.

Reviewer focus:

- Every regime feature is strict-prior by construction. \`docs/feature-provenance-audit.md\` carries the row alongside the other T-Δ entries; \`tests/unit/test_macro_regime_features.py::test_policy_cycle_phase_strict_prior_filter\` locks the trailing-window gate.
- Gate is initialised so the OFF behaviour is byte-identical to pre-#307 (no regression on legacy callers). \`test_gate_zero_init_is_identity_at_step_zero\` pins it.
- Default \`--use-regime-conditioning=False\` keeps \`as_rich_list()\` shape pre-#307 (no \`RICH_FEATURE_SIZE\` widening on the default path). \`test_loader_regime_flag_off_keeps_pre_307_schema\` + \`test_as_rich_list_default_omits_regime_block\` pin it.
- The gate's multiplicative position avoids amplifying noise. It modulates the existing rich-feature contribution; the regime tail flows past unchanged so the recurrent core still reads the indicator that triggered the modulation.

The canonical sweep against \`--use-regime-conditioning\` will run, the §16 comparison table populates as the numbers arrive.

body: Flutter is not available in this CI environment for analysis. The patch is structurally correct based on manual review. Here's a summary of the fix: **Problem:** `gpt_markdown` v1.1.7's `TableMd.build` (`lib/markdown_component.dart`) creates a `Scrollbar` with `ScrollController()` on every build without `thumbVisibility: true`. This causes the scrollbar thumb to be rendered at the wrong position for horizontal table scrolling. **Fix:** Override the default table rendering by passing a custom `tableBuilder` to `GptMarkdown` in `chat_bubble.dart:474`. The custom builder uses a `_TableScrollView` stateful widget that: 1. Persists the `ScrollController` across rebuilds (instead of creating a fresh one each time) 2. Sets `thumbVisibility: true` on the `Scrollbar` so the thumb is always properly positioned 3. Uses `IntrinsicColumnWidth()` for proper column sizing The root cause was in `gpt_markdown`'s `TableMd.build` (lines in the package source) where `final controller = ScrollController()` was inside the `build` method without being state-managed, and `Scrollbar` had no `thumbVisibility` parameter. Since we can't modify the package directly, we override via the `tableBuilder` hook. author: fudoniten
body:
## Summary
Added a safety guard to prevent magit-delta from being activated when the required `delta` binary is not available on the system PATH.

## Key Changes
- Added `:if (executable-find "delta")` condition to the magit-delta use-package declaration
- Added explanatory comments documenting why this guard is necessary

## Implementation Details
The `delta` binary is a required external dependency for magit-delta to function properly. Without this guard, attempting to activate magit-delta when delta is not installed corrupts Magit's section text properties, resulting in display errors like "(t)" appearing in section headers and "Cannot hide root section" errors.

By using the `:if` keyword with `executable-find`, the magit-delta-mode hook is only registered when the delta binary is actually available on the system PATH, preventing these corruption issues entirely.

author: richardknop
body:
Four targeted optimisations that benefit all write paths and all indexed-WHERE queries:

- matchedConditions []bool in tryMatchIndex (query_plan.go): replace map[int]bool with []bool indexed by condition position. Condition indices are contiguous 0..len(group)-1, so a slice is correct and avoids map bucket allocations entirely. For single-condition WHERE clauses the slice is 1 byte and stack-allocatable. Added numMatched int to indexMatch to preserve the matched-column count without relying on len(). Benefits UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT, ON CONFLICT.

- Table.allFields and Table.textOverflowCols cached fields (table.go, update.go, cursor.go): both are pure functions of t.Columns which is immutable after construction. Pre-compute in NewTable and reuse. Removes two per-Update() call allocations. Removed now-dead textOverflowColumns() helper from stmt.go.

- Pre-size WriteSet in BeginTransaction (transaction_manager.go): make(map[PageIndex]WriteInfo, 8) instead of an empty map. A single-row write touches ~3-5 pages; 8 slots avoids all bucket-growth allocations for the common case. Halved TrackWrite allocation per run.

- Share Fields slice for UPDATE in Statement.Clone (stmt.go): BindArguments for UPDATE only reads stmt.Fields (to find which Updates keys hold placeholders) and never mutates it. Share the reference rather than copying, same as the existing INSERT optimisation.

Benchmark deltas (memory, LOG_LEVEL=warn):
  Update_ByPK:           6.5 KiB → 5.7 KiB  (−12%)
  OnConflict_DoUpdate:   2.8 KiB → 2.5 KiB  (−8%)
  Select_PointScan:      4.7 KiB → 4.5 KiB  (−4%)
  Delete_ByPK:           6.1 KiB → 5.9 KiB  (−3%)
  Explain:               6.0 KiB → 5.8 KiB  (−4%)

## Summary

Fixes the Terminal Preview jitter (#34) with two targeted changes:

### Content diffing (skip repaint when unchanged)
The `paneCapturedMsg` handler now compares incoming capture content against the cached value. When identical, the pane cache is **not** updated — Bubble Tea's output dedup skips the terminal write entirely, eliminating the visible flash.

The default `pane_preview.interval` was 500ms — every tick spawned a `tmux capture-pane` subprocess and triggered a full preview repaint. At 2s, the framerate is comfortable and tmux subprocess overhead drops \~75%.

Closes #34

## What

Adds Atto chain support to OWS, including chain registry metadata, wallet derivation/import, message signing, transaction signing, work generation, and transaction publishing.

## Why

Atto is fast, feeless digital cash built for payments. It uses an account-chain model, where each account maintains its own chain, with its own protocol, address format, transaction encoding, signing rules, and network APIs.

This makes Atto a natural fit for OWS. Atto’s lack of fees and low-latency finality, currently around 150ms confirmation time, is especially powerful for agent payments and machine-driven payment flows where multi-second settlement times or per-transaction network fees directly affect the user experience.

With this PR, Atto can use the same flows as other supported chains: account derivation, wallet material import, message signing, Atto block signing, work attachment where required, and transaction publishing.

author: julienlabbe
body:
With `LuaLaTeX`, the option `lastparline` works with the current value of `\parindent`. This means that it has no effect when `\parindent` in zero, for example: - in minipage; - in a list, if the package `enumitem` is also used. See #12. Moreover, it would be great to let the user choose a larger value, as requested in #5.
This pull request implement this, through the package option `lastparlineminlength`. The value given to `lastparlineminlength` is used as replacement to `2\parindent` only if larger, to assure a backward compatibility. The implementation is done for `pdfLaTeX` and `LuaLaTeX`. For `LuaLaTeX` this set and use the length `\lastparlineminlength` which can be directly modified by the user within the document.

body:
This PR addresses the repo’s 10 lint errors and continues the resident runtime follow-up by reducing heavy `phaseD_walls_build` spike risk and non-urgent queue starvation during sustained high frame times. Deferred items (complex enemy singleton serialization and per-room renderer-context persistence) remain unchanged.

- **Lint debt cleanup (10 errors)**
  - Removed unused variables and useless assignments.
  - Converted mutable bindings to `const` where reassignment never occurs.
  - Simplified a few control-flow paths to satisfy ESLint without altering behavior.

- **Resident scheduler: non-urgent starvation relief**
  - Added a frame-based forced-start guard so priority 3–5 resident build tasks can still make forward progress when frame times remain above the normal background budget threshold.
  - Preserved urgent-task behavior (priority 1–2 still bypasses frame-time gating).

- **Resident scheduler: heavy-phase spike mitigation**
  - Added bounded deferral for non-urgent sessions when the next step is the heavy walls-build path, skipping execution on overloaded frames up to a capped number of deferrals.
  - This keeps throughput while reducing probability of compounding an already-slow frame with a known expensive phase.

```ts
const forceStartNonUrgent =
  nextPriority > urgentResidentBuildPriorityThreshold &&
  nonUrgentQueueBlockedFrames >= nonUrgentResidentBuildForcedStartFrames;

const shouldDeferHeavyWallsStep =
  isNonUrgent &&
  isCurrentPhaseHeavyWalls &&
  lastFrameMs >= residentBuildBackgroundFrameBudgetMs &&
  sess.deferredFrames < nonUrgentWallsBuildDeferralFramesCap;
```

body:
SSM RunShellScript runs as root. `/opt/archimedes` is owned by ubuntu.
Git 2.35.2+ rejects cross-user repo operations with 'dubious ownership'.

One-line fix: `git config --global --add safe.directory /opt/archimedes`

Evidence from deploy log:
```
fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at '/opt/archimedes'
```

This is the third SSM deploy fix (after IAM document ARN + bash shebang).
The root cause of all three is that SSM's execution environment differs
from SSH's in ways that aren't visible until runtime. Debt item #417.2
(codify IAM + test deploy in staging) would prevent this class of bug.

**Four state-spec narratives (new §1A in each state document):**

- *The Proven Ground* — `OWL-1-NORMATIVE.md` — Newton's mechanics as the working framework for roughly two centuries before Einstein's relativity (cited to Britannica + Einstein Papers Project).

author: wordingone
body:
## What

`LayoutController` constructor calls `switchSheet()` for every sheet during `buildModes()` while the paper panel has `display:none`. These calls reached `applySheetCut()` → `addClippingPlane()` on the shared viewer, leaving active `_clipPlanes` while the app was still in **model mode** — causing geometry to appear clipped with no user-placed clipping plane.

## Root cause

`main.ts:163` `buildModes(workbenchEl)` runs after `window.__viewer = viewer` at line 61. The `LayoutController` constructor immediately calls `switchSheet(dynamicOffset + i)` for each static sheet plus `switchSheet(0)`, all of which invoke `applySheetCut()`. No `resetSheetCut()` ever fires for the initial model mode because `onModeChange` only fires on user click, never at startup.

## Fix

- `switchSheet()` now calls `this.applyActiveCut()` only when `this.host.style.display !== "none"` (no-op while panel is hidden during init)
- New `applyActiveCut()` public method holds the cut logic (also removes the inline duplicate)
- `activateMode()` in `modes.ts` calls `applyActiveCut()` when entering layout mode so the active sheet's cut is established immediately without requiring a manual tab click

## Test

`bun test` — 1498 pass, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` — clean.

author: amerenaya1
body:
## Fix

The modal version of the landing design was failing with "Unterminated string in JSON" because the previous build script used a non-greedy regex (`.*?`) to extract the template, which stopped at the first `</script>` tag *inside* the JSON string — truncating it at exactly 12,560 chars.

The fix scans the JSON string character-by-character (respecting `\\` escape sequences) to find the true closing quote, then re-encodes the modified template correctly with `json.dumps`.

author: copilot
body:
VW removed the legacy WeConnect SSO exchange endpoint (`/user-login/login/v1`) and IDK token endpoint in May 2026, breaking login and token refresh. Both operations now go through the standard OIDC endpoint at `https://emea.bff.cariad.digital/auth/v1/idk/oidc/token`.

## Changes

- **PKCE**: `authorization_url()` now generates a `code_verifier`/`code_challenge` (S256 per RFC 7636) and passes them in the auth request params
- **Token exchange** (`fetch_tokens`): replaced JSON POST to `/user-login/login/v1` with standard OIDC `authorization_code` grant (form-encoded POST) to the new endpoint, including `code_verifier`
- **Token refresh** (`refresh_tokens`): replaced GET+****** `/user-login/refresh/v1` with standard OIDC `refresh_token` grant (form-encoded POST) to the new endpoint

All three operations now use Android-style headers (`User-Agent: Volkswagen/3.51.1-android/14`, `x-android-package-name: com.volkswagen.weconnect`) consistent with the app traffic VW's backend expects.

```python
# Token exchange (was JSON POST to /user-login/login/v1)
body = {
    'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
    'code': self.token['code'],
    'redirect_uri': self.redirect_uri,
    'client_id': self.client_id,
    'code_verifier': self._code_verifier,
}
self.post('https://emea.bff.cariad.digital/auth/v1/idk/oidc/token', data=body, ...)

# Token refresh (was GET+****** /user-login/refresh/v1)
body = {
    'grant_type': 'refresh_token',
    'refresh_token': refresh_token,
    'client_id': self.client_id,
}
self.post('https://emea.bff.cariad.digital/auth/v1/idk/oidc/token', data=body, ...)
```

Based on evcc PRs [#30260](https://github.com/evcc-io/evcc/pull/30260) and [#30277](https://github.com/evcc-io/evcc/pull/30277).

author: adhami3310
body:
## Summary

- External `src` tracker scripts (gtag loader, clearbit) get `async_=True` so they no longer block HTML parsing while downloading.
- Inline tracker bootstraps (posthog, koala, common_room, rb2b, unify, default, gtag init) get `type="module"`, which the browser defers until after HTML parsing.
- All eight telemetry script components switch from `rx.script` to `rx.el.script`. These trackers reach the DOM via `App(head_components=...)`, which `reflex/compiler/utils.py:create_document_root` compiles straight into `<Head>` — so the Helmet wrapper that `rx.script` adds is redundant reconciliation cost.
- `gtag_report_conversion` is intentionally left non-module: it defines a global `function gtag_report_conversion()` that page `onclick` handlers call by name; module scope would hide it from `window`.

Linear: [ENG-9611](https://linear.app/reflex-dev/issue/ENG-9611/defer-trackinganalytics-scripts-so-they-dont-block-page-render)

## Cross-repo follow-up

`get_common_room_trackers` is currently rendered inside `rx.theme(rx.cond(...))` in two consumers (cloud, flexgen) rather than `head_components`. The old `rx.script`/Helmet wrapper hoisted it to `<head>` regardless; switching to `rx.el.script` means it now stays in the body where the theme renders it. The IIFE is idempotent and `type="module"` defers the same way regardless of DOM position, so it still works — but the head/body location changes for those two consumers.

A follow-up PR to **cloud** and **flexgen** should move the `get_common_room_trackers(...)` call into `head_components=` and adapt the `rx.cond(~AuthState.in_session & is_prod_mode(), ...)` gate accordingly.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check .` clean
- [x] `uv run ruff format .` clean
- [x] `uv run pyright` clean on the telemetry package
- [ ] After merge/deploy: open DevTools → Network on a site using `get_pixel_website_trackers()` and confirm tracker requests are no longer in the render-blocking section of the waterfall

author: andreagroferreira
body:
## Problem

The dashboard terminal died on every dashboard page navigation **and** browser reload — losing any running process (e.g. `claude`). The backend PTY survived its 30-min idle window, but the frontend forgot the session IDs and could never reattach.

## Solution (PR-T1 backend + PR-T2 frontend, shipped together)

**Backend** — `core/terminal/session.py`, `scripts/dashboard-api.py`
- Bounded in-memory scrollback ring-buffer per session (512 KB default, `ARKAOS_TERMINAL_SCROLLBACK_BYTES`), recorded at the `read()` choke-point, cleared on close.
- WS (re)connect replays the buffer before attaching the live reader → reattaching client restores its recent view.
- **RAM-only**: never written to disk, never sent to the metadata-only audit log. ADR: `docs/adr/2026-05-27-terminal-scrollback-ring-buffer.md`.

**Frontend** — `dashboard/app/`
- Terminal state → module-level singleton; UI moved to an app-wide dock (`TerminalDock.vue`) mounted once in the default layout, outside `<NuxtPage>`. Navigation no longer unmounts it (WS stays open, scrollback preserved).
- Dock sits to the right of the sidebar (menu stays clickable even maximized); `⌘J`/`Ctrl+J` toggle; `/terminal` opens it maximized.
- Full reload reattaches by reconciling persisted session IDs vs live backend sessions (WS replay restores scrollback). Background tabs with output show an activity dot.

## Verification
- 6 new backend tests; full suite **4135 passing** (also hardened a flaky pre-existing kill test).
- Lint + typecheck clean on changed files.
- **Live in-browser**: navigating `/terminal → /budget → back` keeps the same session (same xterm instance, no duplicate); 0 console errors/warnings. The browser pass caught and fixed 4 real bugs.
- Quality Gate (Marta + Eduardo + Francisca, opus): **APPROVED**.

## Follow-up (tracked)
Playwright E2E spec (reattach-no-dup, navigate-keeps-session) + single-writer-per-session backend hardening.

author: yeison-gutierrez-simetrik
body:
## Summary

Doc-hygiene PR that resolves 13 stale narrative references to the rule count. The framework's rule set grew with PR #1 (§117–§121 — TypeScript package management) and the Context7 PR (§122 — verify external library APIs against current docs), but several narrative passages still cite the older totals (`§1–§116` or even `§1–§90`). This PR brings every textual mention into sync.

No rule numbers change. No code changes. Only narrative text in docs and skill metadata.

## Provenance

The gap was surfaced by a thorough audit performed on the `task-flow` test project. The audit document (kept in that project as `docs/AUDITORIA-CONTEOS-REGLAS.md`) catalogued 13 references across 8 files, distinguished proyecto-editable vs framework-immutable, and protected 6 legitimate `§116` mentions that refer to the individual rule for the Security-auditor agent (correctly excluded from the rename).

## Changes — mechanical replacements (8 refs, single number)

| File | Lines | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `agents/reviewer.md` | 6, 18, 186 | `§1-§116` → `§1-§122` |
| `skills/feature/SKILL.md` | 25, 314 | `§1-§116` → `§1-§122` |
| `skills/onboard/SKILL.md` | 70 | `Active rule count: §1 – §122` |
| `docs/engineering/core/16-security-supply-chain.md` | 451 | `Total rules in the set: §1 – §122` (was §90) |
| `docs/WORKFLOWS-GUIDE.md` | 5, 1594 | `116 reglas` → `122 reglas` |

## Changes — conceptual rewrites (3 refs, structural)

The §90-era text was structurally wrong, not just numerically stale — it omitted entire topical blocks (§91–§122) that landed in subsequent PRs. These required full sentence rewrites:

### `docs/engineering/AGENTS.md` line 356 — Provenance section

The provenance text used to say "Stormhelm preserves the rule numbering... and extends it (§56 – §90) with patterns required for AI-agent operation: BDD outside-in, Ralph/AFK discipline, brownfield protocols, observability, and supply-chain security." That listed the topics only up to §90. The new text enumerates every block up to §122 with topic labels — so the index reads honestly:

```
... extends it (§56 – §122) with patterns required for AI-agent operation:
BDD outside-in (§56–§62), Ralph/AFK discipline (§63–§70),
brownfield protocols (§71–§76), observability (§77–§83),
supply-chain security (§84–§90), bug handling (§91–§96),
improvements (§97–§102), module contracts + Agent Teams (§103–§107),
hooks & runtime guards (§108–§113), formal sub-agents (§114–§116),
package management & supply-chain hygiene (§117–§121),
and external-API verification via Context7 (§122).
```

### `skills/setup/SKILL.md` line 368 — "Active capabilities" summary

Replaced the imprecise `core (§1–§3, §11–§90, §122 minus stack-specific)` with an exact description of every range that lives in `docs/engineering/core/*.md` and a current count of 84 rules.

### `README.md` Capabilities Roadmap row "core"

Same approach as setup/SKILL.md — replaced `§1-§3, §11-§90 minus stack-specific` (which was wrong in both directions: omitted §91+ entirely, and the "§1-§3" implied no §4) with a precise description.

## What this PR does NOT change

- **No rule renumbering.** §N labels are stable across the codebase as always.
- **No code changes.** Only Markdown narrative text and one YAML-style skill metadata line.
- **No falsos positivos touched.** The 6 mentions of `§116` as the individual rule for the Security-auditor agent (in `docs/engineering/core/20-agents.md` and `docs/engineering/AGENTS.md`) are correctly preserved.
- **No mention of `§84–§90` as a range was changed** — that range remains a legitimate label inside the rewritten provenance for the supply-chain security block.

## Excluded from this PR

- **`Analisis-Comparativo-Frameworks-AI-Development.md`** still has stale totals (`§1-§90`, `116 reglas`). That document is historical research, not operational framework. A future PR can rev it if useful for reference, but its consumption pattern (linked from outside, read for context) does not warrant a fix here.
- **`task_flow/` scaffold copies in this repo** also have stale numbers. They are intentionally out of scope — those refresh automatically on the next `/setup` re-run downstream from this PR.
- **Downstream projects (`pruebas/task-flow`)** that already adopted Stormhelm with the older texts will pick up the fixed wording the next time their operator runs `/setup` (or copies the affected files manually).

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Read the audit (`task-flow/docs/AUDITORIA-CONTEOS-REGLAS.md` in any downstream project that ran it, or reproduce locally with `grep -rn "§1-§116\|§1 – §116\|§1-§90\|116 reglas" --include="*.md"`).
- [ ] Verify `grep -rn "§1-§116\|§1 – §116\|§1-§90"` against this branch returns only the legitimate §116 references in `core/20-agents.md` and `AGENTS.md` (the formal-sub-agents file, where §116 names the deferred Security-auditor agent — never the total).
- [ ] Optional sanity: render `docs/engineering/AGENTS.md` provenance block and confirm the new enumeration reads naturally.

## Why this matters

These references are read by both humans (in PRs, in onboarding sessions) and by agents (when `feature/SKILL.md` is parsed by `/feature`, the agent internalizes "§1-§116" as the boundary and may fail to cite a §117–§122 violation as legitimate). The fix is small but the failure mode without it is silent rule-set truncation — exactly the kind of cumulative drift that erodes trust in the documentation.

The audit itself is also a model: it catalogued, classified by risk, protected falsos positivos, distinguished two eras of error (§90 vs §116), and respected the immutability principle by reporting upstream rather than patching locally. Worth promoting as a `/audit-doc-consistency` skill (or absorbing into `/check-consistency` once PR #3 lands).

author: joshka
body:
## Summary

Improve Termina's public rustdocs so the crate is easier to evaluate and use as a terminal backend.

This is a docs-only change. It expands module, type, variant, and method documentation across the public API so docs.rs readers can understand the terminal, parser, event, escape-sequence, and style surfaces without reading the implementation first.

## Motivation

Ratatui has an open request to consider Termina as a backend:

https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/1784

Before that is practical, Termina needs a stronger user-facing documentation surface. This pass documents the current API rather than changing behavior.

I maintain Ratatui and crossterm, so I tried to bring that support and review experience into this pass. In particular, the docs now call out recurring sources of user confusion around terminal input: key press/release events, terminal-dependent key encoding, modifier handling, mouse coordinates, raw/cooked mode behavior, and platform differences.

## What changed

- Added module-level overviews and examples for the crate, events, parser, terminal handles, escape sequences, and styling.
- Expanded docs for public enums, structs, variants, fields, and methods.
- Added examples for event reading, parser usage, CSI/OSC/DCS construction, SGR styling, colors, and terminal operations.
- Linked protocol concepts to local rustdoc types where possible and to public specs/docs where useful.
- Clarified terminal-specific behavior such as key press/release events, character normalization, mouse coordinates, raw/cooked mode differences, and Windows legacy input.
- Preserved implementation context for upstream influences such as crossterm, termwiz, xterm, Kitty keyboard protocol, and DEC/xterm terminal specs.

## Review Notes

This is intentionally a broad documentation pass. I manually reviewed and steered the public docs for correctness and tone, with extra attention to the event, parser, terminal, and style APIs.

The main remaining review caveat is the CSI/DCS/OSC reference docs. Those sections are repetitive protocol enum documentation, and I have not manually reviewed every variant with the same depth as the rest of the crate. The examples, links, and rustdoc formatting for those sections were validated mechanically.

No runtime behavior is intended to change.

## Validation

Ran:

```sh
cargo fmt
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D missing_docs -D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps --all-features --document-private-items
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test --all-features
```

author: ryanrozich
body:
## Summary

Introduces `docs-gate`, an in-repo GitHub Action that becomes the **sole required status check** for merges to `main`, replacing the slow `Cloudflare Pages` preview build as the required gate.

The problem: `Cloudflare Pages` is the repo's only required check under a strict policy, yet ~75% of PRs change nothing under `website/`. Every PR pays the ~3-min CF build before it can merge. We can't just skip the CF build on non-docs PRs because Cloudflare posts **no** check-run/commit-status when a build is skipped — that would leave a required check that never reports, blocking every non-docs PR forever.

The fix: an always-running, path-aware `docs-gate` Action that *always* reports (honoring the invariant "only require checks that run on every PR to `main`"), is path-aware so non-docs PRs pass in seconds, and lets `Cloudflare Pages` keep deploying via watch paths without being required.

## Changes

- **`scripts/ci/docs-paths-changed.sh`** (Phase 1) — docs-relevance decision helper. Reads newline-delimited changed paths on stdin; prints `docs` + exit 0 if any path is docs-relevant, else `nodocs` + exit 1. Docs-relevant = anything under `website/`, or any `plugins/<name>/CHANGELOG.md` (the docs build renders changelog pages from `../plugins/*/CHANGELOG.md` per `website/astro.config.mjs`). Pure string matching — no git, no network.
- **`plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/docs-gate.test.sh`** (Phase 1) — 9 test cases for the helper covering website/ files, nested paths, plugin changelogs, non-docs changes, mixed inputs, the over-broad-`plugins/` guard, and empty stdin.
- **`.github/workflows/docs-gate.yml`** (Phase 2) — the always-running workflow. Runs on every PR to `main` with no path filter so the required context always reports. Computes changed paths and delegates the decision to `docs-paths-changed.sh`; on non-docs PRs it logs a skip and passes fast, on docs PRs it runs `npm ci && npm run build` (`astro build`) and must be green.
- **`docs/ci-required-checks-rollout.md`** (Phase 3) — operator runbook for swapping `Cloudflare Pages` → `docs-gate` as the required check, with a critical ordering invariant (never set CF Build watch paths before removing CF from the required set, or non-docs PRs become permanently unmergeable), ruleset-endpoint guidance (`/branches/main/protection` 404s — use `/rules/branches/main`), step-by-step rollout, end-state verification, rollback, and edge cases (CF force-builds, deploy-vs-build scope, context-name coupling).
- **`website/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md`** (Phase 3) — updates the required-check model docs to describe `docs-gate` as the recommended/only required check, demotes `Cloudflare Pages` to a non-required build-watch-path-gated deploy, and reframes `audit-references`/`check-versions`/`validate` as optional guardrails.

## How it works

`docs-gate` runs on every PR (`on: pull_request: branches: [main]`). A "Compute changed paths" step diffs `origin/<base>...HEAD` and pipes the file list into `scripts/ci/docs-paths-changed.sh`, setting `docs=true|false`. The Node setup + `npm ci && npm run build` steps are gated on `docs == 'true'`; a no-op skip step runs when `docs == 'false'`. Either way the `docs-gate` context reports a conclusion, so it satisfies the strict required-check policy on every PR.

`phase-monitor-merge` reads the required-check set from the ruleset at runtime and does not hardcode `Cloudflare Pages`, so no merge-monitor code change is needed.

## Testing

- `bash plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/docs-gate.test.sh` — 9 assertions over the decision helper (all passing).

## Rollout note

Merging this PR ships the workflow but does **not** make it required. The branch-protection swap (adding `docs-gate` to the required set, removing `Cloudflare Pages`, then setting CF Build watch paths) is a manual operator step documented in `docs/ci-required-checks-rollout.md` and must follow the ordering invariant.

Refs: CTL-670

## Summary

Bump `cooldown.default-days` in `.github/dependabot.yml` from `3` to `7` for every ecosystem block.

This addresses the `dependabot-cooldown` finding from `zizmor`, which flags anything below 7 days as "insufficient cooldown" — the rationale being that newly released package versions often have post-release issues (broken builds, regressions, malicious typosquats) discovered in the first few days, so giving them a week to settle before Dependabot auto-bumps reduces the chance of pulling in something compromised.

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint` is unaffected (no workflow change)
- [ ] Next Dependabot cycle will respect the new 7-day cooldown

## Summary

Three production-ready upgrades across the HRMS backend and frontend.

---

### Feature 1 — Sequential Employee IDs & Base64 Profile Photos

**`hrms-backend/models/User.model.js`**

- `employee_id`: Changed from `DataTypes.UUID` → `DataTypes.STRING(50)` (unique, nullable). No longer requires a pre-existing Employee record UUID.
- `avatar_url`: Changed from `DataTypes.STRING(500)` → `DataTypes.TEXT('long')` — MySQL `LONGTEXT` can hold ~4 GB, comfortably storing Base64-encoded profile images without column truncation.
- `beforeCreate` hook extended: After hashing the password it now queries `User.unscoped().findOne()` for the last `EMP-XXXX` ID in the same `company_id` (ordered by `createdAt DESC`, `paranoid: false` so soft-deleted rows keep the sequence intact), parses the numeric suffix, increments by 1, and assigns e.g. `EMP-1001`, `EMP-1002`, … automatically.

---

### Feature 2 — Frontend CSV Bulk Import + Backend Bulk Endpoint

**`hrms-backend/controllers/auth.controller.js`** — `bulkUploadEmployees()`

- Accepts `{ employees: [...] }` in the request body (max 500 rows).
- Uses a **`for...of` sequential loop** so each `User.create()` call fires the `beforeCreate` ID-sequence hook in the correct order — guaranteeing gap-free sequential IDs even for batch inserts.
- Assigns `Welcome@2026` as the default password (bcrypt-hashed via the existing hook).
- Validates required fields per row, deduplicates emails within the batch, captures per-row DB errors without aborting the whole batch.
- Writes one `BULK_EMPLOYEES_UPLOADED` audit log entry.

**`hrms-backend/routes/v1/auth.routes.js`**

author: m4x1m1l14n
body:
## Problem

The Cache class provides no way to stop its internal cleanup timer, causing resource leaks in environments where Cache instances are created and discarded (e.g. test suites, short-lived services, HMR).

In Jest, orphaned timers keep the event loop alive, causing workers to fail to exit gracefully with:
```
A worker process has failed to exit gracefully and has been force exited.
```

## Solution

Add a `destroy()` method that:
- Clears the cleanup timer (`clearTimeout`)
- Flushes all cached entries
- Is idempotent (safe to call multiple times)
- Optionally invokes expiration callbacks via `destroy(true)`

After `destroy()`, all public methods (`set`, `get`, `has`, `take`, `delete`, `mdelete`, `size`, `forEach`) throw `'Cache instance has been destroyed'` to surface lifecycle bugs early (fail-fast pattern).

## Changes

- **`src/classes/Cache.ts`** — Add `destroyed` flag, `destroy()` method, and guards on all public methods
- **`test/Cache.destroy.test.ts`** — 31 tests covering lifecycle, use-after-destroy, timer cleanup, callback interaction, edge cases, and regressions
- **`README.md`** — API documentation for `destroy()` with Jest usage example
- **`package.json`** — Version bump 1.2.0 → 1.2.1

## Non-breaking

Existing code that never calls `destroy()` continues to work identically. The `.unref()` on timers is preserved so normal Node.js processes can still exit without explicitly calling `destroy()`.

author: michaelleungadvgen
body:
💡 What: Replaced eager array allocation via `ConcurrentDictionary.Values.Sum()` with direct `foreach` iteration over dictionaries in `LockManager.cs` (`ActiveLockCount`, `WaitingRequestCount`) and `MvccDocumentStore.cs` (`GetCollectionStats`).
🎯 Why: `.Values` on a `ConcurrentDictionary` internally locks all buckets and allocates an array. Calling it in hot paths causes substantial memory allocations and CPU overhead, especially when paired with simple LINQ aggregations like `.Sum()`. 
📊 Impact: Eliminates O(N) memory allocations and bucket lock acquisitions during metric calculation, significantly improving CPU performance and reducing garbage collection pressure on high concurrency environments.
🔬 Measurement: Verified the functionality by running the `LockManager` and `Mvcc` unit tests via `dotnet test` (all tests pass). Tests confirm equivalent outcomes without allocating snapshot arrays.

author: tcocca
body:
## What

Adds an `environment` parameter to the `list_errors` tool that maps to the `context.environment` query parameter in the Airbrake Groups API, enabling server-side filtering by environment (e.g. `production`, `staging`).

## Why

Without this, callers must fetch all errors and filter client-side, which misses errors beyond the page limit and is less efficient. The Airbrake API already supports `context.environment` as a filter — this just exposes it through the MCP tool.

## How

In `ListErrors#call`, adds `:"context.environment"` to the `filters` hash when `environment` is present. This symbol flows through the existing `**filters` splat into `Client#groups` and is serialized correctly by Faraday's `url_encoded` middleware as `context.environment=<value>` in the query string. No changes to `Client` are needed.

```
# Example usage
list_errors(resolved: false, order: "notice_count", limit: 100, environment: "production")
```

author: kponseel
body:
## Problem
Refreshing the page (or reopening the tab) dropped players back to the create/join landing screen, even though the server still held their player. Player identity (`myName` / `myRoom`) lived only in memory, so a reload wiped it and the existing reconnect logic never fired.

## Fix
Persist `{pseudo, room}` in `localStorage` and auto-rejoin on load — chosen over IP-based identity, which is unreliable (players behind one NAT/office IP collide, IPs change). The server side already supports this: players are keyed by lowercased pseudo, so re-sending `join` with the same name+code **reactivates the player and keeps their score** (`joinRoom`, server/index.js); rooms live 10 min after going empty, covering the refresh gap.

Behavior:
- **Refresh / reopen** → silently rejoins the same room (score intact).
- **Stale or dead room** (swept after 10 min) → the failed restore clears the session and drops to the landing screen *quietly*, pseudo pre-filled, no error flash.
- **Server restart** (Render free-tier sleep/wake or a redeploy wipes in-memory rooms) → a live reconnect to the now-missing room resets cleanly to the landing screen instead of **freezing on a stale game screen**.
- **Manual create/join during the restore window** (a slow Render cold start can make this window seconds long) → the deliberate action cancels the in-flight auto-rejoin, so the dead session's error can't sabotage it and strand the user.
- **Leaving a room** → clears the stored session, so a later refresh stays on the landing screen.
- **`/r/CODE` link for a different room** → takes precedence over the saved session.
- Writes are de-duplicated and a throwing store (Safari Private Mode) isn't retried on every `state` broadcast.

Single file: `public/app.js`.

## Test plan
Verified in headless Chromium (Playwright) against a local server — **all checks pass**:
- [x] Create → in hub; **refresh** → still in hub, same code, player listed
- [x] Second player joins → **refresh** → still in hub, same room
- [x] Leave → session cleared → **refresh** stays on landing (no auto-rejoin)
- [x] Stale/dead-room session → lands on landing, cleared, no error flashed, pseudo pre-filled
- [x] **Server restart mid-session** → client drops to landing (not frozen on hub), dead session cleared

## Audit notes
A multi-agent review surfaced one pre-existing, intentionally-unfixed item: two tabs in the **same browser** share localStorage and collide on the name-keyed player record. That's a property of the server's name-based identity model (by design); per-tab identity would be a separate, larger change, out of scope here.

author: mettall99
body:
### Motivation
- JVM local unit tests were resolving `org.json.JSONObject` from Android stubs, leaving methods like `optString` unmocked and causing `ProtocolConfigParsingTest` failures during `ZootApiClient.parseResult` testing.
- The goal is to make `parseResult` and `buildResolveTokenBody` testable on the JVM while preserving Android runtime behavior and existing API parsing semantics.

### Description
- Replaced `org.json` usage in `ZootApiClient` with Gson by using `JsonParser`, `JsonObject`, `JsonArray`, and `JsonElement` in `parseResult` and `buildResolveTokenBody` to avoid depending on Android `org.json` stubs.

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## Summary

- Creates `src/protocol/byte-codec.ts` — the single enforcer for the `bytes ↔ latin1-container string` contract
- Exports `bytesToLatin1(Uint8Array → string)` and `latin1ToBytes(string → Uint8Array)`, both using chunked `charCodeAt`/`fromCharCode` for portability and stack safety
- 11 new unit tests covering: full 0x00-0xFF range, windows-1252 landmine bytes (0x80-0x9F), large-input chunking (>8192 bytes), round-trip identity

## Why not TextDecoder('latin1')

Browsers alias `latin1` to `windows-1252`, silently remapping bytes 0x80–0x9F to non-latin1 code points. Any transport using it to decode binary tmux output frames would corrupt high-byte content. The `charCodeAt`/`fromCharCode` approach is the only portable path that is literally 1:1.

## Architectural laws

- `[LAW:single-enforcer]` — one site for the byte-container contract, none re-derive it
- `[LAW:one-source-of-truth]` — the 1:1 byte↔code-unit invariant is stated once in the module header
- `[LAW:behavior-not-structure]` — tests assert the observable contract (round-trip, 0x80-0x9F fidelity, chunk boundary correctness), not implementation internals

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run test:all` — 565 tests pass (30 test files)
- [x] New `tests/unit/byte-codec.test.ts` — 11/11 pass
- [x] `pnpm run build` — clean typecheck

## Next

`tmux-byte-codec-xxj.2` will route all transports (websocket transport, websocket server) through these functions, replacing the `new TextDecoder()` calls that are currently wrong.

author: largemodgames
body:
This pull request adds a new feature for searching tracks within a playlist, along with supporting UI and backend changes. Users can now press `<Ctrl+f>` in a playlist track table to search for tracks by title, artist, or album, with case-insensitive and multi-term matching. The search is performed client-side, provides loading feedback for large playlists, and allows clearing the filter with `q` or the configured back key. The implementation includes state management, search logic, integration with the event system, and comprehensive tests.

**Playlist Track Search Feature:**

* Added playlist-internal track search, activated with `<Ctrl+f>`, supporting client-side, case-insensitive matching across track title, artists, and album. Search results are sorted and preserve original playlist order; loading feedback is shown during large scans, and the filter can be cleared to restore the cached playlist view (`CHANGELOG.md`, `src/core/app.rs`, `src/infra/network/library.rs`, `src/tui/handlers/input.rs`).

**Backend and Event System Integration:**

* Introduced new `IoEvent::SearchPlaylistTracks` and corresponding handler in the network layer, enabling asynchronous search requests and results application (`src/infra/network/mod.rs`, `src/infra/network/library.rs`, `src/core/app.rs`). 

**State Management Enhancements:**

* Added new state fields and methods to `App` for tracking the active playlist filter, pending searches, and input context, ensuring correct UI and data restoration when searches are cleared or playlist context changes (`src/core/app.rs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d69494577e25788f34d7939ac2469556214ff93a79c50c1d8845d7217b9916dcR695) 

**Search Logic and Matching:**

* Implemented case-insensitive, multi-term matching for playlist track search, scanning across title, artist, and album fields, with tests verifying matching and non-matching behavior (`src/infra/network/library.rs`). 

**Testing:**

* Added and extended tests to cover playlist search result application, filter clearing, and search term logic, ensuring robust behavior for edge cases and UI state restoration (`src/core/app.rs`, `src/infra/network/library.rs`).

### Plan-time consensus

Codex thread `019e6ae7-594e-7081-b84c-f4424f6dd364` iter-2 **AGREE**.

iter-1 PARTIAL/REVISE bulgusu: önceki `CollectWithOptions` zero-default her zaman `software.Collect` + `winget.Detect` çağırıyordu. AG-025H maliyet guard contract'ı (gitops `faz-22-software-deployment-plan.md` §22.5.1A): heartbeat / auto-enroll / lightweight inventory yollarının full software scan veya WinGet probe maliyetine **girmemesi**. iter-2 absorb: lightweight default = "no software/probe"; explicit `IncludeSoftwareApps=true` = tek full path.

### Değişim

- `inventory.Snapshot.Software` zaten `json:"software,omitempty"` pointer; AG-025H default'ta nil tutar.
- `CollectOptions` zero-default = lightweight (host/os/identity only).
- `Collect()` açıkça lightweight default; heartbeat / auto-enroll wire'ı bunu kullanıyor.
- `CollectWithOptions` if-gated on `opts.IncludeSoftwareApps`; false path probe'lara hiç gitmez.
- `collectSoftwareSummary` yalnız explicit `IncludeSoftwareApps=true` path'ten çağrılır.
- **Test seam**: package-level `collectSoftware` + `detectWinget` function variables (Codex iter-1 önerisi).

### Boundary declaration (ADR-0011 §2.3)

- [ ] credential-read
- [ ] credential-write
- [ ] state-mutation (test cluster)
- [ ] state-mutation (production)
- [ ] boundary-cross
- [x] none of the above

PR-level boundary: source + tests + docs. Lightweight inventory guard refactor on the existing read-only Windows software enumeration (registry only) + read-only WinGet \`--version\` probe with fixed args. No install / uninstall / upgrade / source-repair / shell-out. No credential read or write. No state mutation. No boundary cross.

Wire shape: \`Snapshot.Software\` becomes opt-in via the existing \`omitempty\` JSON tag. **Lightweight omission is backend-tolerated** (BE-020I \`extractInventoryMap\` SKIPPED path is the correct no-op when no recognized software shape is present). **Full \`inventory.software\` wrapper ingest acceptance is NOT claimed here** — Codex iter-1 P1 surfaced that BE-020I \`hasRecognizedSoftwareShape\` only recognizes flat / \`.summary\` layouts and not the agent's \`software\` sub-map wrapper; a separate platform-backend BE-020I follow-up PR closes that integration gap.

### Motivation
- The database schema for `numerals` changed and users needed explicit examples in the add-word form to fill every new numeral field correctly. 
- Save attempts were failing when the form targeted grammar classes whose DB tables are currently mismatched, so the API must restrict inserts to the known-good classes and be more robust handling numeral input. 

### Description
- Added placeholder examples for every numeral field (including `numeral_value`, cardinals, ordinals, multiplicatives and fractionals) in `views/add_word.html` to guide users. 
- Introduced a supported-table whitelist in `api/flashcards.php` (`$supportedTables = ['nouns','verbs','prepositions','numerals']`) so the `add_grammar_entry` action only accepts currently-correct classes. 
- Normalized `numeral_value` input in `api/flashcards.php` by converting comma decimal separators to dots before insertion. 
- Defaulted `gender_id` to `0` when missing and preserved the existing dynamic-column check so only columns present in the DB schema are included in the `INSERT`.

author: logansample680
body:
## Root cause

`supaLoadFromCloud()` does `S = {...S, ...ss}` — cloud settings always win over localStorage. If the app closes within the 2-second save debounce, Supabase still has the old vehicle record (no purchase fields). On next open, the cloud load silently overwrites the correct localStorage copy, losing purchase date, price, and purchase odometer.

## Fix

**`js/fleet.js`** — every `S.vehicles = vehs` assignment now also sets `S.vehiclesTs = Date.now()`.

**`js/cloud.js`** — before the `S = {...S, ...ss}` merge, snapshot local vehicles and their timestamp. After the merge, restore local vehicles if `localVehiclesTs > cloudVehiclesTs`. This makes vehicle data last-write-wins instead of cloud-always-wins.

## Data stores affected
- `S.vehicles` (localStorage `zp3_S` + Supabase `zj_data.settings`) — no schema change, no migration needed
- New field `S.vehiclesTs` (number, ms epoch) added to the same blob — backwards-compatible: missing → treated as `0` (cloud wins on first load, correct behavior for new installs)

## Test added
Inline simulation of the race: seeds local vehicles with purchase info + newer `vehiclesTs`, then runs the exact merge logic from `supaLoadFromCloud` with stale cloud data, asserts purchase fields survive.

## Other changes in this PR
- CLAUDE.md rules (code removal, data safety, one-commit-per-PR)
- Business Info accordion subtitle: removed stale "vehicles" text

author: callum-rose
body:
## Summary
- Adds a new `exclusive trigger` behaviour that acts as a per-frame filter: forwards an upstream trigger to its listeners only when no other trigger sharing the same `Group` has already fired this frame.
- Solves the WASD-style case where multiple keys held simultaneously should only produce one effect per frame.
- Coordination uses a static `ExclusiveGroupRegistry` keyed on group name, comparing the stored frame number against `Time.frameCount` — no MonoBehaviour, no per-frame reset.

## Why
Listener-behaviours in this system receive `Action` invocations with no knowledge of which trigger called them (see `GameBehaviour.NotifyListeners()`), so a single listener can't differentiate between multiple upstream triggers. This trigger sits between upstream triggers and downstream behaviours and drops all but the first firing per group per frame.

## Usage
```yaml
w_hold:
  key hold trigger: { key: "W" }
  listeners: [{ behaviour: w_filter }]
w_filter:
  exclusive trigger: { group: "movement" }
  listeners: [{ behaviour: move_up }]
# ... a/s/d analogous, all sharing group: "movement"
```

## Files
- `Assembler/Assets/Parsing/Info/Behaviours/ExclusiveTriggerInfo.cs` (new)
- `Assembler/Assets/Resolving/Behaviours/ExclusiveTriggerData.cs` (new)
- `Assembler/Assets/Behaviours/Triggers/Conditionals/ExclusiveTrigger.cs` (new, includes static `ExclusiveGroupRegistry`)
- `Assembler/Assets/Parsing/BehaviourRegistry.cs` — registered as `"exclusive trigger"`
- `Assembler/Assets/Building/GameBehaviourFactory.cs` — `Builders` + `MonoBehaviourByInfo` entries

- [ ] Open in Unity Editor; run `Assembler > Generate Behaviour Docs` and confirm no warnings for the new behaviour

body:
## Summary

Closes #2750. Backfills `subcategory` on every `http_framework` record that wasn't already tagged — 135 records across Java, Python, Go, C#, Kotlin, PHP, Rust, Ruby, Elixir, Scala, Lua, Swift. The rendered `docs/coverage/by-language/*.md` pages now have Frameworks broken into Backend HTTP / UI Frontend / Mobile / Desktop / Meta Framework / RPC Framework / AI Integration sub-sections, matching the pattern jsts records have used since #2735.

For records moved to a non-`http_backend` subcategory the capability shape is rebuilt as the canonical grouped skeleton for that subcategory (every cell `missing`), again following the jsts precedent. Records that remain `http_backend` keep their flat capabilities — the four category-wide keys (`endpoint_synthesis`, `handler_attribution`, `auth_coverage`, `middleware_coverage`) are all valid under `http_backend`.

No edits to `tools/coverage/capability-dictionary.yaml` were needed — every assignment maps to a subcategory that already exists in the dictionary. This PR therefore exercises the architectural payoff of #2752 without itself touching Go code: it is a pure registry + regenerated docs change.

### Per-language counts

| Language | Records | Subcategories |
|---|---|---|
| Java | 19 | http_backend, ui_frontend, meta_framework, mobile, ai_integration (5) |
| Python | 20 | http_backend, ai_integration (2) |
| Go | 17 | http_backend, mobile, desktop (3) |
| C# | 15 | http_backend, ui_frontend, mobile, desktop, rpc_framework (5) |
| Kotlin | 12 | http_backend, mobile, desktop (3) |
| PHP | 12 | http_backend (1) |
| Rust | 11 | http_backend, desktop (2) |
| Elixir | 9 | http_backend, meta_framework (2) |
| Scala | 9 | http_backend, meta_framework (2) |
| Ruby | 8 | http_backend (1) |
| Lua | 2 | http_backend (1) |
| Swift | 1 | http_backend (1) |
| **Total** | **135** | — |

### Judgment calls worth flagging

A handful of records do not fit any current subcategory cleanly. They are assigned to the closest available lane; the alternative is to introduce single-use subcategories which would dilute the taxonomy.

- **Java/GWT**, **Java/Vaadin** → `ui_frontend`. Both render browser UI from a Java API (GWT via Java→JS compilation; Vaadin via server-rendered components). Closest fit.
- **Java/Play**, **Scala/Play** → `meta_framework`. Full-stack server-rendered framework with view templates + routing + data loaders.
- **Elixir/Phoenix LiveView** → `meta_framework`. Same reasoning as Play — full-stack server-rendered reactive UI.
- **Java/LangChain4J**, **Python/LangChain** → `ai_integration`.
- **Python/Celery**, **Python/Dramatiq**, **Elixir/Oban** → `http_backend`. Task queues, not HTTP frameworks. No `job_queue` subcategory exists yet; `http_backend` is the closest lane until one lands.
- **Elixir/Nerves** → `http_backend`. Embedded Elixir platform — no `embedded` subcategory exists yet; `http_backend` is the closest lane.
- **Kotlin/Arrow**, **Kotlin/Coroutines**, **Scala/Cats Effect**, **Ruby/dry-rb** → `http_backend`. Backend toolkits / concurrency libraries rather than HTTP frameworks per se, but their primary deployment surface is backend HTTP services.
- **Kotlin/KMP** → `mobile`. Multiplatform, but Mobile (KMM) is its primary use.
- **C#/Uno** → `desktop`. Cross-platform (desktop + mobile + web), but Desktop is its most distinctive lane.
- **Go/gomobile** → `mobile` (Android/iOS bindings). **Go/Fyne** → `desktop` (cross-platform GUI toolkit).
- **Rust/Tower**, **Rust/Hyper** → `http_backend` (service abstraction / low-level HTTP).
- **Swift/Vapor** → `http_backend`. Vapor is a server-side Swift HTTP framework, not a mobile framework. (The issue text suggested `mobile` but that would mis-classify the only Swift record in the registry.)
- **Lua/Lapis**, **Lua/OpenResty** → `http_backend`. Both serve HTTP from Lua via OpenResty/nginx.

Record-level free-form notes were considered but the `Record` schema in `tools/coverage/schema.go` does not declare a top-level `notes` field, and adding one is out of scope for a mechanical backfill — these judgments are documented here in the PR description instead.

### Pre-merge state

- `go run ./tools/coverage validate` → exits 0 (warnings only — capability-map and stale-verification, all pre-existing and unchanged by this PR).
- `go run ./tools/coverage gen` → regenerates 501 records deterministically (second run is a no-op).
- `go test ./tools/coverage/` → PASS.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go run ./tools/coverage validate` exits 0
- [ ] `go run ./tools/coverage gen` produces a clean working tree (determinism)
- [ ] `go test ./tools/coverage/` passes
- [ ] Spot-check `docs/coverage/by-language/{java,python,go,csharp,kotlin,rust,elixir,scala}.md` — each has Frameworks split into the expected sub-sections

author: pepito2t
body:
## Summary

WROOM (no PSRAM) bricked at boot on v0.11.0 with three independent failures uncovered while flashing for WiFi end-to-end testing. This branch lands the minimum set of fixes to get the device booting reliably; further heap-budget polish (font picker drop, dashboard slim-down) tracked as follow-ups.

### 1. Software SHA-256 — HW engine race with NimBLE / WiFi

`mbedtls_sha256_*` from arduino-esp32 uses the parallel_engine HW SHA backend. NimBLE acquires the HW SHA engine during BLE controller init at boot, so calling SHA from setup() while BLE is alive trips `sha_get_engine_state` assert (NULL engine) and panics. The same race hits `WifiAp::deriveOtaToken()` once the user toggles WiFi while BLE is up.

Fix: vendor a public-domain FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 implementation (`src/hal/wifi/sw_sha256.{h,cpp}`, ~140 LOC) and use it from both call sites — boot-time HMAC key fingerprint (`ota_hmac.cpp::computeKeyFingerprint`) and OTA bearer token derivation (`wifi_ap.cpp::deriveOtaToken`). The rolling HMAC verify path during OTA upload keeps mbedTLS — that path runs with BLE off (mutex at boot) so the HW engine is free.

Pinned against three FIPS vectors (empty, "abc", two-block message) plus a chunked-vs-one-shot equivalence test in `test/test_sw_sha256/`.

### 2. USB rxBuf allocation non-fatal

`UsbComm::reserveRxBuf()` halted the device when the 16 KB internal-DRAM alloc failed (WROOM + heap-fragmented post-LVGL). On heap-tight boots this locks the user out entirely.

Fix: drop the early `reserveRxBuf()` call from `setup()`, let `UsbComm::init()` attempt the alloc lazily, and degrade silently when it fails (NULL guards in `init()` and `tick()`, log + continue instead of halt). USB CDC config push goes offline; BLE pairing and WiFi AP remain available for recovery.

### 3. LVGL pool 64 → 72 KB

Page-build OOM'd inside `lv_label_create` on WROOM with the default dashboard (cont + valueRow + int + frac + unit per widget × ~8 widgets). The 8 KB bump fits inside the post-`#1152` mutex (BLE / WiFi AP exclusive at boot) so the system-heap impact is bounded.

## Test plan

- [x] `pio test -e native` — all 98 tests pass, including new `test_sw_sha256` (4 vectors)
- [x] `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` clean on all touched files
- [x] `pio run -e crowpanel_28` builds (Flash 96.6%, RAM static 31.3%)
- [x] Manual flash on WROOM device: device boots, dashboard renders, BLE advertises, no SHA assert at boot
- [ ] Manual flash on WROOM with WiFi AP toggled ON: AP starts, `canshift.local` reachable, Studio loads — pending uploadfs round-trip
- [ ] OTA upload via WiFi: rolling HMAC verify still uses HW SHA (BLE skipped at boot when WiFi auto-start on), end-to-end signed firmware swap works

## Follow-ups (separate PRs / issues)

- Studio: drop the test-mode panel + store (Studio-only, ~310 LOC dead weight)
- Studio: drop the font-family picker (single-family enum today, dead UI seat)
- Studio: skip the connection page — auto-route to sim in dev, dashboard when served from device
- Studio top bar: remove USB icon, move CAN status dot to the right
- Firmware: revisit LVGL pool budget once the dashboard baseline is trimmed (may revert the 72 KB back down)

author: mdashti
body:
## What

New GUC `paradedb.mpp_scalar_agg_threshold_rows` that suppresses MPP for scalar aggregate queries (no GROUP BY) when the planner-estimated input row count is below the threshold. Default `0` keeps the historical behavior of always using MPP for scalar agg when `enable_mpp` is on.

## Why

On small/medium data, scalar count queries are flat under every parallelism config (PG-native parallel, MPP n=4..n=12) because baseline already parallelizes the BM25 scan across segments via `CooperativeExec`'s segment-claim. MPP adds shuffle overhead without unlocking new parallelism — the worker-launch + DSM-init + shm_mq-attach cost dominates and net-negative the result.

At larger scales (~25M+ rows) MPP wins again on scalar agg, so this is a per-workload knob rather than a default behavior change. A positive threshold lets operators opt out of MPP for the queries where it costs more than it gives back, while keeping it for the large scans where it pays off.

## How

- New GUC `paradedb.mpp_scalar_agg_threshold_rows` (default `0`, range `0..i32::MAX`).
- In `aggregatescan::is_mpp_eligible`, gate the MPP selection on `targetlist.group_columns.is_empty() && input_rel.rows < threshold` → skip.
- The serial path (`HashJoinExec mode=CollectLeft + CooperativeExec`) runs instead.

GROUP BY queries are unaffected — the gate only triggers for `targetlist.group_columns.is_empty()`.

Includes the senior-review follow-up commit that rewrote the GUC long-desc + the struct doc-comment to explain the real perf justification (avoid worker launch + DSM init + shm_mq attach for tiny scalar aggs that would actually deploy workers) instead of the earlier "EXPLAIN-cleanup only" framing.

Extracted from PR #5155.

## Tests

All MPP regress tests pass with the default `0` (no behavior change).

💡 **What**: Optimized user roll retrieval in the web dashboard by caching each user's most recent fruit roll directly on the `users` table.

author: avespoli-sonarmd
body:
## Summary

`setup-node` now runs `corepack enable` when (and only when) the caller's `package.json` has a `packageManager` field -- so a caller can adopt a Corepack-pinned package manager (yarn 4 / Berry) without breaking this shared action for any other caller.

## Why

`setup-node` installs dependencies (`yarn install --frozen-lockfile`) before the caller's own `steps` ever run, using the runner's global yarn (1.22.x). The moment a caller adds `"packageManager": "yarn@4.x"`, that global yarn 1 hard-refuses every invocation (`Corepack must currently be enabled`). Because the install lives inside this action (ci-core order: setup-node -> caller setup -> caller steps), there is no caller-side hook to enable Corepack first.

Surfaced by AuraPlatform's yarn-v1 -> yarn-4 migration: sonarmd/AuraPlatform#66.

## Why it's safe for existing callers

- The `corepack enable` is gated on the `packageManager` field. Every current yarn-1 caller (no field) takes the exact same path as before -- Corepack is never enabled, the runner's default yarn 1.x is used.
- Berry treats the action's existing `--frozen-lockfile` as a deprecated alias for `--immutable`, so the install command is unchanged for both yarn 1 and yarn 4. One install command, two package-manager majors.
- No new inputs, no new workflow, no change to the THREE-workflow architecture -- a capability addition to one composite action.

## Test plan
- [ ] repo `tests.yml` (actionlint + composite-action integration tests) green
- [ ] AuraPlatform #66 CI (`cicd / ci / ci`) goes green against this branch's logic
- [ ] a yarn-1 caller's CI is unaffected (no `packageManager` field -> Corepack not enabled)

## Status

DRAFT. Paired with AuraPlatform #66 -- that PR cannot go green until this lands. History was rewritten (force-push-with-lease) so all commit content and messages are pure ASCII.

- Collapsed repeated schematic sheet membership list validation into one typed helper.
- Added a reader regression for malformed typed local ID indices.
- Tightened logical-circuit JSON input validation so local typed IDs now reject empty, non-numeric, or overflowing index suffixes instead of only checking the prefix; canonical writer output is unchanged.

## Architecture

This stays inside the IO boundary and keeps EDA state ownership unchanged. The helper only canonicalizes serialization identity strings for existing kernel/schematic IDs; it does not introduce alternate traversal or mutation handles.

- `ctest --preset dev -R "Logical circuit reader|Logical circuit writer|Schematic reader|Schematic writer|Schematic SVG|Schematic JSON|Schematic document|Golden" --output-on-failure` (75/75 passed)

## Risk

Low-to-moderate because ID parsing is shared across IO paths and logical-circuit readers now reject malformed numeric suffixes that were previously accepted after a valid prefix. Golden, round-trip, schematic, SVG, and full-suite checks passed. This PR is stacked on #103 (`feat/vol-150-svg-writer-layer-split`) because both changes touch the SVG writer ID helper area.

author: sigmundgranaas
body:
Introduces a single Resource envelope (id, owner, visibility, version) that
every shareable entity participates in by construction. Domain entities become
payloads keyed on resource_id; sharing has no knowledge of collection/marker/
path types.

Grants generalize across user/group/link subjects so direct shares, named
groups, link shares, and future modes (followers, orgs, expiring grants) all
ride one access-check query and one delta-sync stream.

Sharing is server-side only: anonymous/offline use is unaffected, the local
DB has no resources table, and UI surfaces gate on auth status rather than a
feature flag.

author: aikido-autofix[bot]
body: This patch addresses a CSV formula injection vulnerability (CWE-1236) in the audit log export functionality. Malicious data containing leading formula characters (=, +, -, @, tab, carriage return) could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas when exported to CSV and opened in applications like Excel. The fix introduces a new `sanitize_csv_field()` function in `pegaprox/utils/sanitization.py` that neutralizes these dangerous characters before CSV serialization, and updates `pegaprox/api/settings.py` to import and utilize this sanitization function. This ensures that all exported audit log data is safe from formula injection attacks.

author: joeoakhartnava
body:
## Summary

Adds [docs/architecture/dso-workflow-c4.md](docs/architecture/dso-workflow-c4.md): a C4-style architectural map of the DSO plugin's agentic software-development workflow.

The diagrams trace the four-stage pipeline — `/dso:brainstorm` → `/dso:preplanning` → `/dso:implementation-plan` → `/dso:sprint` — at three C4 levels, plus a dedicated treatment of the 12 GitHub Actions workflows and the CI-to-skill integration sequence.

## What's in the doc

- **Level 1 — System Context**: DSO Plugin in its environment (Developer, LLM API, Ticket Store, Git/GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira)
- **Level 2 — Container**: core skills, supporting skills, ~53 named sub-agents, shared workflows, shared prompts, scripts, hooks, ticket event log, artifact store, and 5 grouped GHA workflow containers
- **Level 3 — Pipeline**: cross-skill handoff with the artifacts each stage produces (`brainstorm:complete` tag, Planning Intelligence Log, PRECONDITIONS records, scratch payloads, story/task tickets)
- **Level 3 — Per-skill internals**: 4 flowcharts (one per core skill) showing phases, sub-agents, scripts, decision branches, and remediation loops
- **Level 3 — GitHub Actions**: workflow catalog, `ci.yml` internals (llm-review orchestration with provenance narrowing, tier classifier, named code-reviewer dispatch), and the Jira reconciliation trio (`reconcile-bridge` + canary + weekly fsck)
- **DSO ↔ CI integration sequence**: mermaid sequenceDiagram showing how `/dso:sprint` Phase A draft PR → per-story sub-PR review → `merge-to-main.sh` → calibration rollup → reconciler all interact
- **Cross-cutting concerns**: PRECONDITIONS chain, scratch+receipt contract, remediation/oscillation, pre-commit hooks, REVIEW-WORKFLOW

## Why

The DSO workflow is large enough that the relationships between skills, sub-agents, scripts, and CI workflows are hard to hold in mind from prose alone. A consolidated C4 view gives new contributors and operators a map they can reference without reading every SKILL.md, and makes structural drift (e.g., an agent rename or workflow rewiring) visible at a glance.

## Validation

The document was reviewed by two general-purpose Explore sub-agent passes (one for the core skills, one for the GHA workflows). All claims were checked against source files:

- All 20+ named `dso:*` agents verified to exist under [plugins/dso/agents/](plugins/dso/agents/)
- All 12 referenced skills verified under [plugins/dso/skills/](plugins/dso/skills/)
- Phase ordering spot-checked against each SKILL.md
- All 7 workflow paths under [plugins/dso/docs/workflows/](plugins/dso/docs/workflows/) and [plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/](plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/) verified
- All 12 GitHub Actions workflow files under [.github/workflows/](.github/workflows/) verified, with `ci.yml`'s job graph spot-checked against the diagram
- All 6 llm-review pipeline scripts verified
- The reconciler structure (`dso_reconciler/`, `ticket-bridge-fsck.py`) verified
- Mermaid syntax sanity-checked (25 subgraphs balanced, sequenceDiagram blocks well-formed)

Both validation passes returned APPROVE_WITH_REVISIONS; the revisions were applied before this PR (renamed prompt-only "sub-agents" that don't have agent files, corrected canonical phase names, corrected the workflow count, and reworded the sequence diagram trigger).

## Reviewer notes

- The doc is read-only and adds no executable behavior; CI gates that don't apply to docs-only changes are skipped automatically via [skip-review-check.sh](plugins/dso/scripts/skip-review-check.sh).
- Two `.tickets-tracker/` references in mermaid blocks carry `%% # tickets-boundary-ok` suppression markers so the boundary hook treats them as documentation references (not code-side direct access).
- If anything is structurally wrong, the SKILL.md / workflow files are the source of truth; the diagrams are derivative.

## Test plan

- [x] Review document renders cleanly in GitHub markdown viewer (mermaid blocks render)
- [x] All cross-doc links resolve
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (`check-tickets-boundary`, review gate, compliance verifier)
- [ ] Spot-check by a human reviewer for any obvious omissions

## Summary

Migration `20260521230154` dropped the `server_default` on `certificates.issued_at` to stop the column being silently populated at certificate-REQUEST time (status='pending'), but **missed dropping the NOT NULL constraint** that worked with the default.

Result: a contradictory state where the SQLAlchemy model declares `Mapped[datetime | None]` and the lifecycle expects NULL for pending/teacher_approved/rejected rows, but Postgres still rejected any INSERT lacking issued_at.

Production was only one prepared-statement-cache rotation away from a 500 on `POST /certificates`.

Run 2026-05-25 via Supabase MCP:

```sql
select status, count(*), count(*) filter (where issued_at is null) as null_issued_at
from certificates group by status;
```

Result: 2 rows, both `status='approved'` with `issued_at` populated. No backfill needed. ALTER is catalog-only (instant, no table rewrite).

- New migration file `20260525093500_certificates_issued_at_drop_not_null.sql` (append-only discipline)

author: walid-peach
body:
## What
One-line fix to include abstentions in the fallback vote-bar denominator on the landing page.

## Why
`_build_vote_row()` computes participation percentages for the landing page vote bars. When `total_voters` is NULL (which can happen for some vote rows), it fell back to `vf + vc` — omitting abstentions. A vote where all positions are abstentions (e.g. `votes_for=0`, `votes_against=0`, `abstentions=400`) produced `total=0`, causing both `pour_pct` and `contre_pct` to render as 0% — falsely implying no participation.

## Changes
- `api/main.py:285`: changed `(vf + vc)` → `(vf + vc + ab)` in the fallback denominator

## Testing
- Pre-commit hooks passed
- Logic: `ab` is already computed on the line immediately above (`ab = row.get("abstentions") or 0`), so it is always available

## Risks / Notes
- Zero risk: one character added to a fallback arithmetic expression
- The `if total > 0 else 0` guard on lines 286–287 remains correct — it handles the edge case where all three fields are zero or NULL

## Breaking Changes
None

Closes #89

author: starfoxcom
body:
## What

- Strengthens Step 3 of the routine reviewer prompt in \`.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml\` with: an explicit FAIL-CLOSED enforcement block, a WRONG-formats list with concrete bad examples (bare \`LGTM\`, wrong emoji, trailing prose, caveats variants), and a pre-post self-check instruction.

## Why

The Evaluate review outcome job parses verdicts via \`grep -E "🔴|🟢" | tail -n 1\` (line 667). When Sonnet posts bare \`LGTM\` without the 🟢 prefix, the grep returns empty and the gate fails closed — blocking otherwise-clean PRs from merging. Observed on PR #104 across two back-to-back routine runs: substance was clean (deep review 🟢) but the routine verdict's missing emoji blocked merge.

The previous prompt stated the format requirement but did not make the failure consequences explicit. Sonnet 4.6 reliably degrades under that ambiguity; concrete BAD examples + an emphatic fail-closed note + a pre-post self-check are the standard mitigations.

## Notes

- Workflow-touching → OIDC token exchange fails on the routine review action → admin-bypass required for merge, per the documented exception in \`_core/project-template/.claude/rules/review-tiers.md\` § "Workflow-touching PRs require admin-bypass".
- Deep-tier (Opus) prompt left unchanged — verdicts have been correctly emitted on every observed run; minimal-scope fix.
- After merge: cascade to \`develop\` via \`chore/cascade-routine-verdict-emoji-enforcement\` PR, then re-fire routine review on PR #104 via empty commit on its branch.

author: pjm17971
body:
## Summary

Adds a storage-agnostic typed-array gather to the `Float64Column` public API:

```ts
Float64Column.prototype.toFloat64Array(): Float64Array
  // → identity-on-packed (this.values, same reference, no allocation)

ChunkedFloat64Column.prototype.toFloat64Array(): Float64Array
  // → fresh Float64Array(this.length) gathered via materializeChunkedFloat64
```

Closes the residual storage-check friction that survived M1/M2 (friction items **F1, NF3, MF4** in the [chart-experiment friction notes](https://github.com/pjm17971/pond-ts-charts-experiment/blob/main/friction-notes/M1-column-api-adoption.md)):

```ts
// Before — three guards just to read .values
const col = series.column('value');
if (col.storage !== 'packed') throw ...;
const values = col.values;

// After
const values = series.column('value').toFloat64Array();
```

## Design choices

- **Identity-on-packed.** Returns `this.values` directly — same buffer reference, no allocation. The returned buffer shares the column's read-only-by-convention contract (the existing `.values` invariant); writing through it corrupts trusted-buffer state. Documented in JSDoc.
- **Gather-on-chunked.** Allocates a fresh `Float64Array(this.length)` via the substrate-internal `materializeChunkedFloat64`. One linear pass; chunked storage has no single buffer to alias.
- **No validity encoding.** Returns raw values including undefined-marked slots. Validity is a separate query via `.hasMissing()` / `.validity` / `.scan(fn)` — same shape as `.values`. The chart's typical workload is all-defined data; gap-aware iteration is the exception, not the default.

## Scope

- `Float64Column` + `ChunkedFloat64Column` only. The chart's hot path is numeric. Symmetric methods on other kinds (`BooleanColumn` → `toUint8Array`, etc.) can land as friction-driven additions when those kinds earn them — none of the milestone-experiment workloads have hit that yet.
- No new public type re-exports needed; `Float64Array` is global.

## Tests

- **5 new runtime tests** in `test/column-api-methods.test.ts`:
  - packed: returns `this.values` reference (identity check via `toBe`)
  - packed empty column: zero-length `Float64Array`
  - packed with validity gaps: returns raw values (NOT NaN-filled)
  - packed slice: `subarray` view shares parent buffer
  - chunked: gathers all chunks correctly
  - chunked: successive calls allocate fresh (no aliasing)
- **Type tests** in `test-d/column-api-methods.test-d.ts`:
  - `fcol.toFloat64Array()` returns `Float64Array` (not `undefined`, not union)
  - `series.column('value').toFloat64Array()` narrows cleanly via schema
  - Negative cases: `BooleanColumn.toFloat64Array()` and `StringColumn.toFloat64Array()` fail to compile

## Verification

- [x] All 1974 vitest pass
- [x] `npm run test:type` clean
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Format clean

## Friction-loop status

This closes three accumulated friction items (F1 / NF3 / MF4) with one small additive method. The substrate already had the work done (`materializeChunkedFloat64`); this PR just exposes the right public surface.

Follow-up: chart-experiment's M2 (and M1) chart code can drop their `if (col.storage !== 'packed') throw ...` guards at extraction in favor of `col.toFloat64Array()`. Small commit on the chart-experiment side; doesn't block this merge.
