author: 0pcom
body:
## Summary

#2864 removed the dmsg-pty subtree to consolidate everything under \`skywire app pty <mode>\`, but the standalone \`dmsg\` binary still needs \`dmsg pty <cli|host|ui>\` as its full surface — operators of the standalone binary lost that path with the previous PR.

The intended pattern (and the one this PR implements): **leave the dmsg subtree intact**, and have the skywire-binary import mark the redundant subcommand as **Hidden**. Operator help funnels toward the canonical \`app pty\` path; the old path still resolves when invoked directly.

## What changes

- **\`cmd/dmsg/dmsg/commands/root.go\`** — restore the \`dmsgptyCmd\` group and its AddCommand block. Rename \`dmsgptyCmd → DmsgptyCmd\` (exported) so the skywire-binary import path can set \`Hidden=true\` on it without affecting the standalone dmsg binary.
- **\`cmd/skywire/commands/root.go\`** — after the dmsg tree is mounted, set \`dmsg.DmsgptyCmd.Hidden = true\`. The subtree still works when invoked directly; it just doesn't show up in \`skywire dmsg --help\`.
- **\`cmd/apps/pty/commands/pty.go\`** — the previous version did \`RootCmd.AddCommand(dph.RootCmd, ...)\` which conflicts with the dmsg tree's own AddCommand (cobra can't cleanly handle one Command having two parents). Replaced with **thin delegating wrappers** — \`DisableFlagParsing=true\` forwards all args (including \`--help\`) verbatim to the target's \`Execute\` via \`SetArgs\`. Both \`dmsg pty host\` and \`app pty dmsg\` now coexist without sharing cobra.Command instances.

## Verified

| Invocation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| \`dmsg pty cli\|host\|ui\` (standalone binary) | Visible + functional |
| \`skywire dmsg --help\` | \`pty\` NOT listed (Hidden) |
| \`skywire dmsg pty --help\` (direct) | Still resolves with cli/host/ui subtree |
| \`skywire app pty --help\` | Canonical four-mode listing |
| \`skywire app pty dmsg --no-dmsg --tcp-listen :2022\` | Delegates to dmsg-host RunE with those flags |
| \`skywire app pty tcp --addr :2022\` | Equivalent to above |

## Test plan

- [x] \`go vet\` same scope clean
- [x] gofmt clean
- [x] Smoke test: all five invocations above behave as expected
- [ ] CI lint

author: critterwilson
body:
## Summary

Fresh-eyes Opus-level review of JACOB. Found two **P0** minor-safety bypasses in the delegated-membership model (ADR 0015); both are fixed inline in this PR. The full review with all P0–P3 findings is in `OPUS_REVIEW.md` at the repo root.

### P0 fixes shipped here

- **P0-1: `PATCH /api/users` no longer accepts `isMinor`.** A user could sign up truthfully as a minor, then PATCH `isMinor=false`, then bypass every owner-escalation gate. `isMinor` is now off the patch surface entirely (`extra=forbid` rejects the key); the only legitimate value comes from the DOB-derived computation at onboarding.
- **P0-2: open-mode self-join now escalates minors to owner review.** `joinMode == "open"` (the default) used to run a transparent self-join with no minor check, letting a minor self-join any open-mode group. The branch now checks `isMinor` first and falls through to the request-mode (owner-escalation) path when the caller is a minor — symmetric to the invite-consume minor path in `groups.py:join_group`.

### P0 regression tests
- `test_update_profile_rejects_self_minor_flip` — PATCH with `isMinor` returns 422.
- `test_minor_open_mode_join_escalates_instead_of_self_joining` — minor + `joinMode=="open"` lands a pending join-request with `requiresOwnerReview: true` instead of self-joining.

### Small P2 fixes also included
- `firestore.rules` comments: ADR 0014 → ADR 0015 (ADR 0014 is push notifications; ADR 0015 is delegated membership).
- `backend/Dockerfile`: comment referenced `daily_verse.py` which was removed in #350.
- `infra/scheduled/cleanup_stale_devices.py`: dead `users_ref` variable removed.

### Deferred (in `OPUS_REVIEW.md`)
- **P1-1** Read DOB from the private profile in minor-decision endpoints and re-derive `isMinor` — defence-in-depth against a future drift bug.
- **P1-2** Refuse minor leader applications; surface `isMinor` in the owner queue.
- **P1-3** SSE listener-attach failure leaves the connection hung — broadcast a sentinel so the client falls back to polling immediately.
- **P1-4** Legacy fcmToken-only dedup still spawns duplicate device docs for pre-installationId clients.
- **P1-5** Production cutover gaps: apphosting.yaml hardcoded to staging, empty prod project, no Terraform applied, no Secret Manager values, no runbook.
- **P1-6** Make `"request"` the default `joinMode` (current default is `"open"`).
- Plus P2 / P3 nits.

### Verification
- `backend` unit tests: 954 passed, 0 failures.
- Frontend never PATCHes `isMinor` (verified — the only caller, `settings/profile/page.tsx`, only sends display/phone/location/faithBackground).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (lint + type-check + tests + frontend)

body:
Close: #437
Here's a summary of what was created and refined:

The requirements cover 7 areas for the SAC Asset Compatibility Matrix:

Asset Identification & Normalization — canonical form rules for XLM (native) and SAC tokens (alphanum4/12), with idempotence and whitespace trimming. Added explicit rejection for empty codes and codes over 12 characters.

Supported Asset Validation — whitelist enforcement against the registry, with precise error types (UnsupportedAssetError), case-sensitive matching after normalization, and XLM's issuer-agnostic treatment.

Decimal Handling & Amount Normalization — 7-decimal-place canonical format with explicit half-up rounding, boundary values (min 0.0000001, max 1000000), and rejection of zero/negative/non-numeric inputs with INVALID_AMOUNT.

Transfer Semantics Consistency — payment link format, memo sanitization, and metadata (assetType/assetIssuer) behave identically for XLM and SAC tokens.

Fee Routing Consistency — equal fees for equal inputs regardless of asset type, no per-asset formula variations, and decimal mismatch rejection with state preservation.

Rejection of Unsupported Assets — all rejections surface as 400 Bad Request with ASSET_NOT_WHITELISTED, with a concrete definition of a valid Stellar public key (56-char base32 starting with "G").

Test Coverage — positive and negative tests for all critical operations, idempotency tests, and data-driven registry extensibility.

body:
## Summary

Redesigns `tools git commits` to fix four reported issues and add standup-friendly output:

1. **Workitem IDs** — No repo change to default patterns; per-user `~/.genesis-tools/git/config.json` tightened to `\d{5,6}` (backup at `config.json.bak`). Footer no longer lists 1–4 digit phantom IDs.
2. **Branch attribution** — Cascade: `name-rev` → trunk filter → `branch --contains` (workitem-aware) → reflog rescue → trunk-only `[trunk: …]` fallback → `(detached)`.
3. **Rebase / dates** — Patch-id dedup (newest committer wins), authored vs rebased-into-range split, compressed cluster footer (B.0 truncation, never `+1 more`), optional `--include-rebases` with `[authored …]` tags, `(?)` reset-author hint.
4. **Grouping & columns** — `--group-by day|branch|workitem|none`, inline `[branch]` / `[#id]` by default, `--markdown` / `--clipboard`, `--with-workitem-title` via `enrichWorkItems`.

New modules under `src/git/lib/`: `format`, `branch-attribution`, `patch-id-dedup`, `rebase-classifier`, `markdown-render`.

author: smartbalanced-sgc
body:
## Why this PR

Six live cycles since 2026-05-26, every one returned 0 BUYs. Three operator critiques:
1. "Refuse parabola" kept firing on names that kept rallying — threshold wrong for current market
2. "The AI narrative is full of jargon, I don't understand a thing"
3. "Surface the AI catalyst findings in the dashboard — tokens are already spent anyway"

Plus FMP burst test confirmed parallel-4 is safe on Starter plan (40 reqs / 13s = 3 req/sec, zero 429s).

## Five fixes in one PR

### 1. Parabola thresholds raised
| σ-class | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| MID | 0.50 | **0.80** |
| HIGH | 0.80 | **1.50** |
| EXTREME | 1.00 | **2.00** |

Calibrated for AI-cycle continuation regime. MU (+92%), ARM (+99%), INTC (+94%), MRAM (+182%), RKLB (+98%) no longer auto-refused. Sacred #18 still in force — just at realistic thresholds.

### 2. Friendly verdict display names

| Internal CSV value | Display name |
|---|---|
| REFUSED-PARABOLA | **OVEREXTENDED** |
| REFUSED-EV | **EV-NEGATIVE** |
| REFUSED-METHOD | **MATH-CONFLICT** |
| REFUSED-TREND | **DOWNTREND** |
| BELOW-THRESHOLD | **CLOSE-CALL** |

Internal `verdict_state` in CSV unchanged (backward compat). Dashboard only.

### 3. Plain-English AI surfacing in detail row

Before:
> "Q1 earnings, magnitude high, direction_risk bullish, date 2026-05-27"

After:
> "📰 Q1 earnings beat (2026-05-27) — strong signal, likely to push price UP"

With verdict-contextual framing (PER operator instruction "make sure what's surfaced is complete and not misleading"):
- **BUY**: "Math says: take this trade many times, you'd make money on average. AI findings support."
- **EV-NEGATIVE**: "Math says average outcome below safety bar. AI sees factors below, but statistical downside outweighs."
- **OVEREXTENDED**: "Stock rallied so much that mean reversion is higher-probability. Engine refuses to chase."
- etc.

Uses CSV data already collected (pass2_catalysts_json, pass2_agreement, narrative_score) — zero additional AI tokens spent.

### 4. max-parallel default 2 → 4

Empirically safe per FMP burst test (40 reqs, 3 req/sec sustained, no 429s). Plus `_fmp_get` retries once on HTTP 429 with Retry-After honoring, then degrades gracefully to None. Cycle doesn't fail on transients.

### 5. Detail-row labels in plain English
- "DIRECT entry @ $X" → **"Option 1 — Enter now at $X"**
- "WAIT-FOR-DIP @ $X" → **"Option 2 — Wait for dip to $X"**
- "P(rally hits)" → **"Chance rally hits in 20 days"**
- "EV (unconditional)" → **"Average return per trade"**

## Tests

`tests/test_pr89_thresholds_renames_ai_surface.py` — 11 new cases including:
- Thresholds raised + true blowoffs still refused (sanity guards)
- Verdict display name mapping
- Plain-English catalyst translation
- Per-verdict framing context
- `_fmp_get` retries on 429, returns None on persistent failure
- max-parallel default verified via `--help` output

**612 / 612 tests pass.**

## Operational impact next cycle

- MU/ARM/INTC/MRAM/RKLB flow through to EV evaluation instead of auto-refusing
- Dashboard reads like a guide for a new investor, not an SEC filing
- Cycle wall-time ~50% faster (parallel-4)
- 429 transients don't crash subprocess
